articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's Week 11 lineup advice
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone breaks down the Week 11 slate and provides his top lineup tips.
articles.body:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 11 rankings.

Prescott is coming off a five-touchdown performance and a QB1 overall finish (tied with Patrick Mahomes) in Week 10. It was his fourth consecutive game with multiple scores and his second straight with over 330 passing yards.

Another big stat line is on the way against a Titans team that went from bad to worse after trading away two of its best players, Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker. In its last two outings, Tennessee has given up 462 yards and five touchdowns to Joe Burrow in Week 8 and 352 yards and three TDs to Trevor Lawrence last Sunday.

The Cowboys are also projected for the most points of the week at 31.5. That's partially due to the elevated play volume between these two clubs. The Titans and Cowboys are first and second in neutral pace of play, setting up a busy day for both offenses.

Bo Nix vs. Raiders – Prior to the Broncos' Week 10 bye, Nix quietly finished as a fantasy QB1 in three straight contests. Now, he'll take on a Raiders defense that's the fourth-easiest matchup for passers, allowing at least two touchdown passes to each of the last eight passers they've faced.

Cam Ward at Cowboys – Ward will be on the other side of the high-volume affair between the Cowboys-Titans, battling a Dallas defense that's the third-most generous to quarterbacks. With Ward stating that he feels comfortable in no-huddle, the team is now using it at one of the highest rates in the league. The results speak for themselves, with Ward posting his two best fantasy outings of the season recently, finishing as the QB4 and QB12.

Coleman's playing time and rush share have increased in every contest during his impressive rookie campaign.

Since returning from injured reserve, he has played 49% of the snaps and handled 50% of the carries against the Cardinals, 66% of the snaps and 61% of the carries versus the Chiefs and season-highs with 77% of the snaps and 81% of the runs in a win over the Panthers prior to Denver's Week 10 bye.

Next up is a Raiders defense that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to RBs, the second-most rushing yards and the fourth-most rushing touchdowns.

With the Broncos entering the game as 10.5-point favorites, there should be plenty of positive game script for Coleman to rack up stats en route to a fantasy RB1 finish.

Tony Pollard at Cowboys – Pollard has been on fire lately, posting 155 scrimmage yards and three TDs against the Browns, 137 yards and two scores versus the Bengals and 99 yards and a TD on a tough Jags' front. Now, he gets a revenge game against a Dallas defense that's giving up the most fantasy points to RBs.

Breece Hall at Chargers – Hall has been solid since returning from his five-game injury absence, notching 87 yards and 108 yards, respectively, over the last two outings. In fact, Hall is averaging over 100 scrimmage yards in the four contests he's played that weren't impacted by the injury. The Chargers are allowing the 12th-most fantasy points, including double-digit points to seven different RBs in their last seven games.

Omarion Hampton vs. Jets – Hampton finally came to life with his first 100-yard effort of the season in Week 10. There hasn't been much that's gone right for the Chargers this season, so I'd expect them to lean into Hampton's recent success. That should be easy to do against a Jets defense that's the eighth-friendliest opponent for fantasy RBs.

Tate has missed the last two outings due to a shoulder injury, but fortunately he's on track to return for this shoutout. And as you can tell, we're starting almost everyone in the Titans-Cowboys game.

Prior to getting hurt, the rookie saw at least seven targets in four of his last five appearances, while posting quality stat lines of 6-58-0, 9-145-0, 6-70-1 and 5-69-0.

With Tate sidelined, Wan'Dale Robinson, Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor all posted notable stat lines with Tennessee pushing the pace on offense. But now Robinson is out for the year with an ankle injury.

If Tate can avoid the trainer's table as well, he'll have a chance to post his best fantasy day yet in an uptempo contest against a Cowboys defense permitting the fifth-most points to receivers.

Rashee Rice vs. Cardinals – Even with Josh Downs joining the mix, Rice still led Chiefs receivers in targets, yards and receptions last week. He's now delivered double-digit fantasy points in four of his last five healthy games. He remains a solid fantasy WR2 in a plus matchup with Arizona.

Jaylen Waddle vs. Raiders – If you don't want to start a wideout who's only gone over 40 yards twice all season, I understand. Just know that the Broncos had the second-toughest schedule for fantasy WRs in the first nine weeks and now have the 12th-easiest moving forward. That starts with a Raiders defense giving up the seventh-most fantasy points to his position, the seventh-most receiving yards overall and the most receiving touchdowns.

Ryan Flournoy vs. Titans – Flournoy has put up at least 50 yards and/or a touchdown in six straight games and finished as a top-24 fantasy WR in five of those outings. Meanwhile, the Titans are the best matchup for receivers in 2026. Even as the third pass-catcher in Dallas, Flournoy can be started in fantasy as a WR3/flex option.

Since Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury, Okonkwo has averaged the eighth-most targets among tight ends and turned in three games with over 50 yards in five outings.

Okonkwo likely would have accomplished that feat last week as well, had it not been for a back injury that caused him to miss part of the contest. With Okonkwo not playing his usual snaps, backup Ben Sinnott turned in four catches, 42 yards and a touchdown.

As long as he can stay on the field, Okonkwo is set up well this week against a Bengals defense that's the ninth-best matchup for fantasy tight ends.

Mark Andrews at Panthers – The arrival of tight end whisperer Jacoby Brissett helped Andrews to his first game over 50 yards all season. The veteran caught all eight of his targets for 82 yards against the Chargers and admitted after the game that he's been playing through a broken hand since Week 3. That puts him back in the low-end TE1/high-end TE2 conversation.

Mike Gesicki at Commanders – Gesicki's lack of volume is frightening, with just one or two targets in four of his last five games. However, the Bengals have the fourth-highest implied point total on the week and we know he has a nose for the end zone after scoring six touchdowns already this season. Washington is a good matchup for tight ends and receivers, so regardless of how you categorize him, Gesicki is a streaming option.

Young's early-season surge was assisted by a soft schedule through the first six weeks. Over the last month, when the schedule became more difficult, Young has struggled more often than not, getting held to 209 passing yards and one touchdown or less in three of his last four appearances.

That stretch has also coincided with offensive line injuries that have had a negative impact on Young and the Panthers' passing attack.

It's difficult to trust Young in a below-average matchup with the Ravens and it's not going to get better in the coming weeks. Carolina has the second-toughest slate the rest of the way, including dates with the Buccaneers, Vikings, Steelers and Seahawks before the end of the fantasy season.

Brock Purdy vs. Vikings – While it feels wrong to have Purdy in the sit section, the degree of difficulty will be at its highest level in Week 11. Brian Flores' defense is the worst matchup for fantasy QBs by far, allowing nearly two fewer points per game than the second-place Seahawks. Minnesota has held each of the last eight passers its faced under 14 fantasy points, including Josh Allen.

Jared Goff vs. Buccaneers – Tampa's defense is allowing the fourth-fewest points to quarterbacks and Goff has struggled against them the past two seasons. Goff finished as the QB21 and QB25 in those contests while only throwing one touchdown and three interceptions.

Since returning from injury, Barkley has managed to salvage his fantasy stat lines with a touchdown in three straight contests. However, his efficiency has been in sharp decline with just 30 rushing yards on 13 attempts in Week 8 and 22 yards on 13 carries in Week 9. He's also only seen one target in each of those outings, so you can't bank on receiving work either.

Taking on the Steelers won't help, since Pittsburgh is allowing the third-fewest rushing yards and fourth-fewest rushing touchdowns this season.

It's possible the Eagles could look a little better after having a bye week to regroup, but I'm not trusting Barkley as anything more than a risky TD-dependent, low-end RB2 — even in a week with six teams on bye.

Jordan Mason at 49ers – This isn't the right matchup to start Mason. Over the last month, Mason produces enough yardage in winning game scripts to be in consideration as a fantasy flex. However, in the two losses, he managed only 20 and 35 scoreless yards, respectively. The best path to fantasy RB production against the Niners is as a pass-catcher, which isn't Mason's area of expertise.

Travis Etienne Jr. at Bears – The Saints remain committed to a three-man committee approach, which limits the fantasy potential of all their backs. Etienne has now finished as the RB22, RB36, RB29 and RB40 in his games with New Orleans. Until we see something change, he's just a risky RB3/flex.

Rachaad White vs. Bengals – White wasn't very productive over the last couple weeks and even before that, his best fantasy outings relied on fluky plays. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt nearing a return, White is a low-ceiling flex option.

Samuel has made the most of his touches this year. Despite being held to four targets or less in four of his six outings, the 30-year-old playmaker has scored at least 15 fantasy points four times thanks to rushing production, touchdowns and big plays.

While we're never going to take away someone's best plays when projecting their value moving forward, it will be challenging for Samuel to maintain those numbers on so few touches.

The 49ers' receiver depth chart is also getting more crowded with Keenan Allen arriving via trade and Mike Evans nearing a return.

The Vikings are the fourth-toughest matchup for fantasy WRs, so we're bumping down the outlooks for all Niners starters in this game. That makes Samuel a risky WR3/flex this week.

Jalen Coker vs. Ravens – Coker hasn't topped 36 yards in a single game over the last month and is fresh off a zero-catch effort on four targets versus the Saints.

Tre Tucker at Broncos – Tucker continues to be hit-and-miss for fantasy. A matchup with Denver's secondary isn't a spot to chase him this week. Tucker has been held under 10 yards in two of his last three games and the Broncos kept him under 30 yards in each of their encounters last year.

Germie Bernard at Eagles – Bernard hasn't been able to put up more than 30 yards in any of his games over the last month and has failed to reach the end zone during that stretch. With Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson nearing a return, Bernard may have missed his window.

Strange was hot in October with at least seven targets in three consecutive appearances. Sadly, that streak came to an end after the Week 7 bye when he's only seen three targets or less per game.

With Jacksonville's ability to control games and take their foot off the gas in the fourth quarter, Strange is a tough click for fantasy.

If this decreased volume continues, you basically have to hope Strange can find the end zone — something he's only done twice this season.

Pat Freiermuth at Eagles – The Steelers tight ends have had one of the easier schedules over the last two months, but that's about to change. The Eagles are the sixth-toughest opponent for fantasy tight ends, which complicates things for Freiermuth since he's only topped 35 yards twice all season.

Darren Waller vs. Ravens – Waller is the ultimate boom-or-bust fantasy tight end. While he offers significant touchdown potential, the floor is zeros across the board. So, I'll let you decide if you want to start a player who has three catches or less in seven of his nine appearances this season.

articles.title: How Ferris State Found Itself At The Center Of The College Football Universe
articles.summary: The calls, the planning and the excitement behind Big Noon Kickoff's historic trip to Ferris State. Here's how it all came together.
articles.body: The message was unmistakable. "THE NATION IS WATCHING," read the big white letters stretching across an electronic billboard along US-131, the highway connecting Grand Rapids to Big Rapids, Michigan. A scowling Ferris State bulldog occupied the left side. The FOX Sports "Big Noon Kickoff" logo sat on the right. It was a welcoming site for Rob Stone, Matt Leinart and members of the "Big Noon Kickoff" pregame crew, who were making the roughly 56-mile drive north from Gerald R. Fort International Airport on Thursday afternoon. When Stone spotted the billboard, he immediately started yelling at the driver to slow down. He wanted a picture, but by the time he was ready to capture it, it had disappeared. So the group spent the rest of the drive glancing out the windows, waiting for it to come around again. Ferris State had put the message on more than 50 billboards across the state, making sure people knew what was coming to Big Rapids. For a university with approximately 8,900 undergraduate students, tucked away in west-central Michigan, it was a declaration of pride in a football program that has won an astounding 41 consecutive games and four of the past five Division II national championships. But this message was about more than the Bulldogs' dominance on the gridiron. For the first time in history, "Big Noon Kickoff" was bringing its traveling college football pregame show to a Division II campus. And the excitement was building by the minute. What followed was a whirlwind few days of anticipation, preparation and coordination between FOX Sports and Ferris State — all leading to a Saturday that neither side will soon forget. Act 1: The Opportunity For Steve Brockelbank, the possibility of bringing "Big Noon Kickoff" to Ferris State first surfaced on a Friday night. The Bulldogs' athletics director was attending a volleyball conference semifinal match when his administrative assistant left a note on his desk. It was time-sensitive, and it instructed Brockelbank to get in touch with Jordan Bazant, FOX Sports’ EVP of business development and media. When he did, Bazant explained that Ferris State was being considered as a potential host for FOX's college football pregame show. He also walked Brockelbank through the economic impact of bringing the show to campus. "I said, 'We would love to have you. Let us know what the next steps are,'" Brockelbank recalled. Across the country — and behind the scenes — Rob Mikulicka, FOX Sports' director of remote studio operations, got word that Ferris State appeared on a short list of potential destinations for the following week’s broadcast. "We were going through options, and Ferris State came up," Mikulicka noted. "We were all like, 'Where is Ferris State? Is this for real?'" But the Division II school stayed in the mix. By Friday night, it was one of the final two candidates. Mikulicka was connected with Ferris State's associate athletics director, Rob Bentley, to discuss what it would take to bring the production to campus. The conversation quickly put him at ease. "Three minutes into the call with Rob, I said, 'OK, we're gonna be fine here,'" Mikulicka said. "They were immediately, just out of the gate, asking, 'What do you need? How can we help you?'" Back on campus, Brockelbank was told FOX Sports would discuss the options over the weekend and have an answer for him either way. He didn't have to wait long. Act II: ‘Buckle Up. This Is Going To Be Big’ Sunday morning, Brockelbank was at home with his family in Ludington, Michigan, enjoying breakfast and getting set to watch the Detroit Lions. Then his phone buzzed. The first message from Bazant was brief: "We are close." A second message followed shortly after. "We're coming to Ferris State." Brockelbank was thrilled. The opportunity he was hoping would come to fruition was suddenly real, and the game, despite his loyalty, had to take a back seat. "I couldn't watch the Lions anymore," Brockelbank said. His attention quickly shifted to what came next. Brockelbank first contacted university president Bill Pink, followed by Bentley. From there, the news made its way to the university's communications and game operations teams. There was plenty of excitement and with that, plenty of nerves. "Are we gonna have the support to pull this off?" Brockelbank recalled wondering. "We weren't necessarily staffed for something of this magnitude." One of Brockelbank's next calls was to Dave Murray, Ferris State's associate vice president of marketing and communications. Murray had been celebrating a memorable weekend as the Bulldogs defeated Roosevelt on Saturday to clinch their third consecutive GLIAC championship. Fireworks filled the sky above Top Taggert Field, where the Bulldogs play their home football games. It appeared the weekend had reached its peak, until Brockelbank called. "Hold on Dave, just when you thought it couldn't get any better, it just did," Brockelbank told him. Murray was dumbfounded. Ferris State was going to host "Big Noon Kickoff" — giving the school a national platform to tell their story. "We were just humbled and overjoyed," Murray said. "It's not just representing Ferris State. It's representing Division II football." Once the excitement died down, the work began. Murray emailed his team with a simple message: "Buckle up because this is gonna be big." It was time for Murray and his team to introduce Ferris State to the nation. Act III: Dad, We’re Going Viral By Sunday evening, the news of "Big Noon Kickoff" heading to Big Rapids was already spreading well beyond the walls of Ferris State. FOX Sports’ announcement of the pregame show going to a Division II powerhouse program generated a massive response across social media. Murray said his Instagram feed felt like the news was featured in nearly every other post. The reaction was overwhelmingly positive, with people across the college football world celebrating the decision to bring FOX Sports' traveling pregame show to Ferris State. For Brockelbank, the response was both exciting and a little surreal. His youngest daughter was the one who first alerted him to just how quickly the announcement was gaining traction. "She was telling me it was going viral," Brockelbank said. He started seeing the numbers climb, along with the conversation taking place across the sport. Later that night, Brockelbank tuned into a Division II YouTube show he often watches, and sure enough, they were discussing the announcement as well.The excitement went beyond social media. On Monday, Murray and members of his team went to the university center to talk with students and get a sense of what they were hearing. It was the talk of the town. Students were making plans to take off work on Saturday so they could attend the pregame show. Later that day, Murray’s team put out a stack of posters and markers, inviting students to make their own signs for the show. By Thursday, a giant stack of posters had been made and ready to be distributed. Some students even took theirs home. Meanwhile, Ferris State was making sure the excitement was felt well beyond campus. Working with one of its billboard partners, Murray’s team designed a series of digital advertisements that began appearing across Michigan on Tuesday afternoon — the same billboard that Stone and the "Big Noon Kickoff" crew came across on their drive from the airport. This was more than a pregame show. More than a football game. It was a moment. A chance for Ferris State University to make sure the rest of the country was watching. Act IV: Feeling The Love By the time the FOX Sports crew arrived in Big Rapids, the preparation was already underway. Mikulicka, who oversees the logistics of moving BNK from campus to campus each week, had arrived in Big Rapids on Sunday night. The following day, he met with Brockelbank, Bentley and representatives from virtually every department at Ferris State to begin working through what was needed to bring the show to life. There were plenty of details to sort out. But any initial uncertainty about bringing the production to a Division II campus was quickly wiped away and put at ease. Everyone involved seemed genuinely thrilled to have the FOX Sports crew in town, welcoming them with open arms. "You just felt the love before you even got into the door," Mikulicka said. "It was a little more special than just a kind of run-of-the-mill show." Stone and FOX Sports’ Big Noon Kickoff analyst Matt Leinart got their introduction to Ferris State Thursday night. The two headed out to experience Big Rapids, beginning with a stop at Schuberg's Bar & Grill. They grabbed burgers and beers, and the owner and chef came over to take a picture with them. Patrons struck up conversations, and even some Ferris State football players stopped by. From there, they made their way to Sawmill Saloon, and finally, an end-of-the-night stop at Star Shooters, which was packed with college students. While out, Stone came across a flyer taped to a giant red door, promoting "Big Noon Kickoff" and everything from hats and T-shirts, to game tickets and a $5,000 prize for the best sign. The town was getting ready for a memorable day ahead. "OK, let's go, the gospel is being spread," Stone recalled thinking. Stone and Leinart were approached by students throughout the night, wanting to know everything about the show, from what they should bring to when they should arrive. "I was just shaking my head and smiling," Stone said. "I think we tapped into something really special and unique." Mikulicka got another reminder of it during a Thursday-night trip to Walmart. Wearing his FOX credential, he was approached by people in the aisles who wanted to thank him for bringing the show to town. "We're gonna show America what we're made of," they told him. When he met with the crew the next morning, he made a point of telling everyone just how special the week had become. Act V: More Than A Show According to Brockelbank, there was a sense of responsibility that came with the opportunity to host "Big Noon Kickoff." The school’s athletics director hoped Ferris State wouldn't be the last Division II school to receive this kind of national exposure. "The one thing I hope comes of this is that you do this somewhere else, at another smaller school," Brockelbank said. "There are so many good stories across the country." Stone shared that sentiment, saying the show has made it a point to devote meaningful time in its rundown to Ferris State, rather than treat the university as a quick stop. "This isn’t just a two-hour program for the university and the football program," Stone said. "This is for Division II football as a whole and for all the other divisions of football that don’t get the love and attention that an Ohio state or Utah or Michigan get on a regular basis." For Mikulicka, the week was also a reminder of why he values the work beyond the logistics of getting a production from one campus to another. After 13 or 14 consecutive weeks on the road, the schedule rarely leaves time to stop and appreciate every experience. "The reason I do this is for the relationships I make with these people," Mikulicka said. "We connect on much more of a personal level. A lot of times when I work with these schools, they are in the same boat I am, trying to figure everything out and how do we do this." He makes a point of writing personal thank you notes to the people who help make each production possible. This week, he had plenty of reasons to do so. Murray, meanwhile, saw the broadcast as a chance to make sure the Ferris State name reached people who might never have otherwise considered the university. "We're a good athletics story," Murray said. "But there are a lot of other smaller schools that are really great in other areas. This is a chance to let people know about it." Forty-one straight wins. Four Division II national titles this decade. This program has already shown what they can do on the football field. Now they have a chance to show the country what Ferris State is all about. articles.title: Who is fifth and final member of Team USA for Survivor Series? Cody Rhodes and CM Punk find their pick on SmackDown
articles.summary: Trick Williams is the fifth and final member of Team USA for Survivor Series: WarGames.
articles.body: Trick Williams is the fifth and final member of Team USA for Survivor Series: WarGames. Cody Rhodes and CM Punk settled the spot on the November 20 SmackDown in Evansville, Indiana. Punk had first put forward Hacksaw Jim Duggan, Rhodes pushed back, and Duggan then said no himself. The United States Champion came out with Lil Yachty, made his own case, and got the nod. Team USA will face Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico on November 28 in Houston. The show ended with word backstage from Nick Aldis that Williams was hurt.Who is the fifth member of Team USA at Survivor Series?Trick Williams got the spot after a detour. Rhodes had told Aldis he would name the pick that night, but Rey Fenix then reported that Punk was already heading to the ring. Punk opened the segment by presenting Hall of Famer Hacksaw Jim Duggan as his pick, and Rhodes was not sold. They went back and forth until Rhodes gave in. A video package on Team Mexico then aired, and Duggan changed his mind. He asked if they still wanted him in the match, said no and left the ring.Williams came out next with Lil Yachty, with Rhodes and Punk still in the ring. Yachty argued the United States Champion deserved a place on Team USA, and the two leaders agreed. All four hugged. Duggan was the sentimental pick. Williams is the practical one, because a champion is a built-in argument.WWE announced the decision online soon after. "Team USA with the United States Champion?!" the post from @WWE said. It went on: "As agreed upon by @CodyRhodes and @CMPunk, @_trickwilliams is the 5th Member of Team USA for Survivor Series!"Team USA's lineup and the Priest attack on WilliamsWilliams then wrestled Damian Priest, with Yachty at ringside. Priest landed early right hands, but Williams answered with a neckbreaker and a clothesline that sent Priest over the top rope to the floor. Williams then threw Priest into the announce table. As Williams set up a big boot, Priest grabbed the ring bell and hit him with it. The referee called for the bell, and Williams won by disqualification.Priest was not done. He hit Williams again after the match, and WWE officials came out to pull them apart. Backstage, Aldis told Rhodes and Punk that Williams is hurt. Both were angry. How serious the injury is has not been made clear, and the spot is not safe until WWE says more.Team USA now has Rhodes, Punk, LA Knight, Je'Von Evans and Williams. Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico has Mysterio, Penta, Rey Fenix and Dragon Lee, with the fifth name still to come. articles.title: Harry Kane to miss ‘a few months’ after injury as Bayern Munich draw
articles.summary: Ballon d’Or winner tears a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne.
articles.body:
England football captain Harry Kane will miss the “next few months” after tearing a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne on Friday.

Kane was taken down in the area by Cologne defender Joel Schmied, who reached Michael Olise’s low cross first but knocked into the Ballon d’Or winner’s left leg in his follow-through at the back post.

Kane writhed in pain. Although he gingerly got back to his feet and initially continued playing, he soon hobbled off the field with two physiotherapists after treatment.

A club statement on X said: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”

Kane is the undisputed star of Bayern. Since joining from Spurs in 2023, he has scored 156 goals in 161 competitive fixtures and won two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup.

He became the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or in 25 years last month and, two weeks ago, signed a new contract with Bayern that will keep him in Bavaria until June 2029.

The night was supposed to be a happy one for Bayern, who welcomed coach Vincent Kompany back to the dugout a month after he collapsed while watching the reserve squad train.

However, Kompany saw his team go behind after just 11 minutes when winger Mikey Moore, on loan from Tottenham, started and finished a counterattack.

Just nine minutes later, Kane limped off to be replaced by Tom Bischof, and the German midfielder made a quick impact. Before halftime, he found Nathaniel Brown, who fired a fierce shot into the bottom corner from the edge of the box.

Both sides had chances in a busy second half but it remained goalless and the point was enough for Bayern to edge a point ahead of Borussia Dortmund. Bayern remained the only unbeaten team in Europe’s top five leagues.

Cologne, for which Moore was named man of the match, climbed one place into 14th.

articles.title: Villamanín vuelve a vender Lotería de Navidad un año después del Gordo que casi rompe el pueblo: "Hace pensar que hay tongo"
articles.standfirst: La comisión de fiestas que vendió participaciones anunció que volverá a jugar este año
articles.summary: La comisión de fiestas que vendió participaciones anunció que volverá a jugar este año
articles.body: Hace casi un año, Villamanín pasó de la euforia a la tensión. El Gordo de la Lotería de Navidad de 2025, el 79.432, dejó en esta localidad leonesa 35,6 millones de euros a través de las participaciones de la comisión de fiestas. Pero pronto se descubrió que 50 de esas papeletas, valoradas en unos cuatro millones, no estaban respaldadas por décimos tras el extravío de un talonario. El pueblo se dividió entre quienes disculpaban el error y quienes se planteaban denunciar. “Hace pensar que hay tongo”, llegaron a decir algunos vecinos. La reunión convocada por la comisión con los agraciados duró más de cuatro horas y estuvo marcada por los gritos e incluso crisis de ansiedad. La solución llegó con un acuerdo de quita para que todos los premiados pudieran cobrar. Los miembros de la comisión renunciaron a su parte del premio, más de dos millones de euros, y los pagos comenzaron en marzo. En abril, la asociación dio el proceso por prácticamente cerrado con un balance “muy positivo”, pese a dos intentos de estafa y una denuncia. Por el camino, comisiones de fiestas de toda España enviaron décimos de la Lotería del Niño en señal de solidaridad. La historia ha inspirado la serie documental ‘El Gordo de Villamanín’, de Movistar Plus, y terminó con un concierto gratuito de Carolina Durante en el pueblo. En junio, en su decimoquinto y último comunicado, la comisión dio una sorpresa: “Este año volveremos a vender Lotería de Navidad”. articles.title: Bad news for Commanders regarding a Laremy Tunsil return in 2026
articles.summary: Don't expect the Commanders to get star left tackle Laremy Tunsil back this season.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders enter Monday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals at 3-5-1. Only recently has it looked like Washington has started to figure things out on both sides of the ball with new coordinators David Blough (offense) and Daronte Jones (defense).

Offensively, things began to unravel on Aug. 8, when star left tackle Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps during a training camp practice. Washington moved Brandon Coleman back to left tackle. Coleman was competing for a starting spot at left guard, so the injury affected two positions.

Tunsil, the NFL's highest-paid offensive lineman, has been around the team while he recovers from his injury. He looks fine. Of course, that means nothing, as he must pass a physical, and a triceps injury is often significant enough to be season-ending.

However, when head coach Dan Quinn spoke to the media this week, he offered an update on Tunsil.

"He had a good last visit, so during the Giants week, he had the next visit with the doctor, and they'll progress into the next phase, which is the beginning of the strength portion," Quinn said of Tunsil.

"So that's some good news. So, if you find yourself in the spots he expected them to be, I think that's good news. But as far as looking away, weeks from now, I think that's too early to call with the exception of good progress and doctors are pleased and ready to begin the next phase. So, I think anytime you're dealing with something, you get onto the next spot, then you're hitting the right things that you need to hit."

You can see why that update got some Washington fans excited, especially if the Commanders are in playoff contention next month.

Tashan Reed of The Washington Post revealed on Friday that Tunsil is not expected to return in 2026.

Reed said that while Tunsil was not expected to return in the regular season, he could play if the Commanders make the playoffs. However, overall, Tunsil's chances of a return are "very slim," Reed noted.

While that's not the news Washington fans wanted to hear, the chances of him returning after a triceps injury in the summer were minimal. It's a significant injury.

Coleman has had his moments in Tunsil's place. While the offensive line has been criticized for much of the season, the unit has played much better in recent weeks. They'll have their hands full with Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen and the Bengals on Monday night.

articles.title: CCA girls sweep, Southern Lee wins two, Lee County splits wrestling matches
articles.summary: Local high school wrestling teams turned in strong performances Thursday night, with Central Carolina Academy’s girls sweeping two matches, Southern Lee winn...
articles.body:
Local high school wrestling teams turned in strong performances Thursday night, with Central Carolina Academy's girls sweeping two matches, Southern Lee winning twice and Lee County splitting its season-opening dual meets.

Central Carolina Academy, Southern Lee compete at Eastern Guilford

Central Carolina Academy traveled to Eastern Guilford for a quad meet featuring North Carolina Leadership Academy and Southern Lee.

The CCA girls dominated their competition, posting identical 18-6 victories over Southern Lee and North Carolina Leadership Academy.

Ryleigh Russell and Isabella Gonzalez led the Eagles, each finishing 2-0. Sydney Stewart and Daphnee Ballenger went 1-1 apiece to help secure the two victories.

On the boys' side, Central Carolina Academy continued to struggle with open weight classes, surrendering valuable team points through forfeits.

Despite the disadvantage, the Eagles battled Southern Lee before falling 36-30.

Charlie Wright led CCA with a perfect 3-0 record. Kevin Spivey Jr. (2-0) and Jean Marie Murry (1-0) also went undefeated, while Ty Couture finished 2-1.

Esau Martinez went 1-1, while Tyler Hunter and Eli Soto each finished 1-2.

Southern Lee finished the night 2-1, defeating Central Carolina Academy 36-30 and North Carolina Leadership Academy 53-24 before falling to Eastern Guilford 69-6.

Southern Lee will compete in the King/Queen Wake of the East tournament Friday and Saturday before hosting a tri-meet Monday.

Central Carolina Academy will travel to North Moore for a 6 p.m. match Tuesday.

Lee County splits season-opening dual meets

The Lee County Yellow Jackets opened their dual-meet season Thursday, Nov. 19, splitting matches against Cary and South Granville.

Lee County fell to Cary 60-24 before rebounding with a 30-23 victory over South Granville.

Against Cary, the Yellow Jackets recorded four victories, including two pins.

Beckham Glasson (144 pounds) pinned Nathaniel Rolon in 26 seconds, while Platon Horner (150) pinned Neil Devkota in 3 minutes, 12 seconds.

Alex Dell (175) and Jancarlo Espinosa (285) each earned victories by forfeit.

Lee County responded with a strong team effort against South Granville to secure its first dual-meet victory of the season.

Liam Kelly (132) pinned Massiah Paylor, while Dell (175) recorded his second victory of the night with a pin over Max Loera.

Kash Lett (157), Victor Rodriguez (190) and Braxton Tickle (215) each picked up victories by forfeit.

Yellow Jackets coach Anthony Dell praised his team's effort and development.

"We have a young team with a lot of potential, and nights like this are important for our development," Dell said. "We saw some things we need to improve, but we also saw our wrestlers compete, respond to adversity, and support one another. I'm proud of the effort and excited about where this team is headed."

Lee County will return to action Saturday, Nov. 21, at the Cecil J. Mock Invitational at Eastern Randolph High School.

articles.title: Bayern Munich star Harry Kane breaks silence with defiant hospital update after undergoing surgery on serious ankle injury
articles.summary: Harry Kane has provided a positive update for fans after successfully undergoing surgery on a serious ankle injury sustained during Friday’s Bundesliga actio...
articles.body:
Harry Kane has provided a positive update for fans after successfully undergoing surgery on a serious ankle injury sustained during Friday's Bundesliga action. The Bayern Munich striker faces a lengthy rehabilitation process away from the pitch following a major blow to the club's silverware ambitions.

The injury occurred during Friday night's 1-1 draw at home against FC Koln . Kane was forced off the pitch as early as the 20th minute after a collision with Joel Schmied. While attempting a shot in the penalty area, the England international was caught on the left foot by the defender's sliding challenge. Although there was no whistle from the referee or intervention from the VAR, Kane's attempt to play on was short-lived as the severity of the damage became clear.

The 33-year-old striker took to social media on Saturday morning to provide an update on his condition following the procedure. Posting a picture from his hospital bed with his left leg in a brace and both thumbs raised, the forward displayed a resilient attitude despite the significant setback. "The highs and lows of life!" Kane wrote on Instagram. "Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!"

During the club's annual general meeting on Saturday, Bayern Munich president Herbert Hainer addressed the situation directly, expressing total confidence in the forward's recovery. He highlighted the mutual respect between the player and the club, noting that while Kane considers it an honour to play in Munich, the club feels the honour is actually theirs to have the World Player of the Year in their ranks.

he club's leadership are rallying around their star man, who has become the focal point of their attack since arriving from Tottenham Hotspur. "We are sure that you will come back even stronger," Hainer stated, as quoted by Sky Germany . "Harry Kane said when he was voted World Player of the Year that it is an honour to play for FC Bayern. The honour is not Harry's, it lies with FC Bayern."

Challenging times for the Munich hierarchy

The loss of Kane for several months represents a major blow to Bayern's silverware ambitions. Sporting director Max Eberl did not hide his frustration after the final whistle on Friday, describing the night as particularly painful for the squad. The injury crisis was further compounded by news that Michael Olise also suffered a foot contusion during the same match, though the French winger is expected to undergo treatment over the coming days rather than facing a long-term absence like his English teammate.

Eberl emphasised that while the situation is incredibly challenging, the team cannot afford to dwell on the misfortune and must find a way to adapt without their leading goalscorer. "This is not an easy situation at the moment. It is very challenging. The evening is very modest, it really hurts us extremely, but we can't lament too much now," Eberl admitted.

Kane now begins a rehabilitation process that will see him sidelined for a significant portion of the current campaign. With the injury involving the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle, the medical team will take a cautious approach to ensure stability before he returns to competitive action. Bayern will be forced to look for internal solutions to fill the void left by the England record goalscorer. As the club navigates a busy domestic and European schedule, the focus will remain on keeping their title hopes alive until Kane is "fresh and ready" to lead the line once again.

articles.title: Orlando Brown Jr says there’s something people don’t realise about Joe Burrow behind the scenes
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle Orlando Brown Jr thinks people don’t get to see just how hard Joe Burrow works and how obsessive he is behind the scenes....
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle Orlando Brown Jr thinks people don't get to see just how hard Joe Burrow works and how obsessive he is behind the scenes.

Burrow is in the middle of an MVP-level season, already notching 2,795 passing yards and 27 touchdowns to help the Bengals go 7-2.

Now, when speaking on Inside the Pocket with Orlando Brown Jr, his teammate has detailed just how much work the quarterback puts in behind the scenes, saying that work and his attention to detail is 'what makes him so great'.

Brown Jr said: "It's the work ethic of Joe Burrow that people are seeing. There's so much that people don't see. You don't see us on the aeroplane while everybody's sleeping and he's watching the tape, asking, 'Hey, man, what were you thinking here? What were you feeling? Hey, this is why I did this. Hey, next time…'

"People don't see that. 'Hey, right here, man, I thought you were going to run him on the field. If you can just…'

"People don't see that, bro. You know what I'm saying? And to me, that's what makes him so great: the work he puts in and his attention to detail."

Joe Burrow's work ethic hasn't changed in six years

Burrow was drafted to the Bengals in 2020 and even as a youngster, his work ethic behind the scenes was catching the eye of his coaches.

Brian Callahan was an offensive coordinator for Cincinnati six years ago and gave a glowing review of the quarterback at the time.

During an interview , he said: "His [Burrow's] offseason work was outstanding. He worked really hard. I think that part gets skipped over a little bit."

Even back then, the now 29-year-old's desire to work hard was having a positive impact on his teammates, with Callahan continuing: "He's such an intense worker. He's put himself in position to know what to do and how to do it. That has rubbed off on his teammates and obviously his presentation and how he goes about his business has been everything we had thought it would be."

Burrow and the rest of the Bengals are now gearing up to face the Washington Commanders on Monday. They have the joint-second-best record in the AFC ahead of the weekend's ties, one win behind the 8-1 Buffalo Bills.

articles.title: USC safety Prophet Brown set for final game at the Coliseum

This week, the USC football team will be back at the Coliseum to take on Maryland . It will be the final home game of the season for the Trojans , who are currently 7-3 on the year and 4-3 in Big Ten play.

In addition, it will mark the final home game for USC's 2026 senior class. One of those seniors is safety Prophet Brown, who has been with the program for a remarkable six years.

"I've watched this program change and transition into what it is today, and it allowed me to see what it takes to create a winning team," Brown said. "That experience has been so great, and I have had so much fun learning throughout that process.

"I know it's rare to see someone in one place for so long, but I'm grateful to be so in love with this team. I hope to be remembered by my team as a caring guy who brought joy and positive energy to everyone in the facility, always with a smile on my face."

articles.summary: Arsenal Team News: Bruno Guimaraes Set for St James’ Park ReturnBruno Guimaraes heading back to St James’ Park is the obvious storyline before Arsenal face N...
articles.body:
Arsenal Team News: Bruno Guimaraes Set for St James' Park Return

Bruno Guimaraes heading back to St James' Park is the obvious storyline before Arsenal face Newcastle on Saturday evening. He left Newcastle for Arsenal in a £75 million move this summer, and this will be his first return to the ground where he built his reputation over four and a half seasons.

There is no mystery about the reception Mikel Arteta wants for his midfielder. Asked whether Guimaraes would get a warm welcome, the Arsenal manager said: "Well I hope so. I think he was one of the main players there and I think he came to the club in a really important part when they had obviously a massive lift in terms of performance and what they have achieved all together, which was really impressive."

Bruno Guimaraes in Arsenal Midfield Spotlight

Sentiment aside, the real issue is selection. Guimaraes has not fully nailed down a regular place in Arteta's starting side, but Martin Zubimendi's hamstring injury changes the equation. Zubimendi is out for "a few weeks", which leaves Arteta weighing up Guimaraes or Myles Lewis-Skelly in midfield alongside Declan Rice.

This feels like a game made for experience. St James' Park is awkward for Arsenal, loud, aggressive and rarely forgiving. Guimaraes knows the ground, knows the mood and knows plenty of the players. That matters.

Arsenal Team News Before Newcastle Clash

Arsenal are still without Bukayo Saka, who is expected to miss another month with a quad problem. Max Dowman remains suspended. Beyond that, Arteta has close to a full squad.

At centre-back, William Saliba is pushing for a return after stepping up his fitness. Ezri Konsa has the shirt for now, and Arteta may prefer continuity here, particularly with Borussia Dortmund coming up in midweek. Giving Saliba controlled minutes in Europe may be the cleaner call.

Noni Madueke should keep his place after a strong run, while Kai Havertz may again be preferred to Viktor Gyokeres in attack.

Predicted Arsenal XI: David Raya, Jurriën Timber, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães, Riccardo Calafiori, Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Noni Madueke, Martin Odegaard, Christos Tzolis, Kai Havertz.

Kick-off is 5:30pm GMT on Saturday, November 21 at St James' Park. For Arsenal, the main call is straightforward enough, trust Bruno Guimaraes in the one stadium where he will not need directions.

articles.title: Philadelphia mayor wants the Eagles to play in a dome
articles.summary: The Eagles will become an indoor team if the mayor of Philadelphia gets her way.
articles.body:
The Eagles will become an indoor team if the mayor of Philadelphia gets her way.

" I want a dome ," Mayor Charelle L. Parker said on 93.3 WMMR, via the Philadelphia Inquirer . "Don't you tell. This is a secret between us. I just saw a rendering of this beautiful dome that they're talking about for the Bears."

Moving into a dome would change the character of late-season and playoff games in Philadelphia, which are often affected by snow, wind and cold. Plenty of fans won't like it. But politicians and NFL owners often prefer stadiums with roofs because they bring in lucrative events, indoor sports, concerts, conventions and trade shows.

The Eagles told season ticket holders last year that they are looking at either renovations to Lincoln Financial Field or a new stadium . Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie has committed only to staying in "the region," not in the city of Philadelphia, but both Parker and Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro have said they want the Eagles to remain in the city.

The Eagles' lease at Lincoln Financial Field runs through the 2032 season.

Relief is finally within reach for the Florida Panthers . After grinding through a punishing early-season travel slate without two of their top offensive catalysts, captain Aleksander (Sasha) Barkov and veteran winger Brad Marchand are nearing the finish line of their respective recoveries. However Florida Hockey Now reports that Barkov will not return for Saturday's game and no word on Marchand

Both forwards have been sidelined with knee injuries since the opening week of the 2026-27 season—Barkov since October 1 against San Jose and Marchand since October 6 against Los Angeles . Following their return to team skates earlier this month, head coach Paul Maurice confirmed that both players have avoided setbacks and are scheduled for final medical evaluations during the team's off day on Friday.

Maurice indicated that they are very close to returning, with Barkov likely tracking slightly ahead due to his injury timeline. This timing aligns perfectly as the Panthers (12-8-3) navigate a homestand at Amerant Bank Arena after a grueling early-season road schedule. The reintegration of Barkov and Marchand—alongside Gadjovich's return to practice—energizes a roster that has heavily relied on depth pieces like Sam Reinhart , Sam Bennett , Anton Lundell , and the Tkachuk brothers .

As the Panthers look to bolster their lineup, the potential return of these key players could provide the spark needed to elevate their performance as they head deeper into the season. articles.title: Clutch overtime 2-point conversion keeps Lake Travis Cavaliers alive in UIL playoffs
articles.summary: Lake Travis used great special teams play and an overtime gamble to beat Cibolo Steele in the UIL high school football playoffs.
articles.body:
SAN MARCOS - There was no doubt for Hank Carter. Or Jason Carter. Or Westin Smith.

If Lake Travis scored a touchdown in overtime Friday, it was going for two and the win .

"Once they scored, we had made the decision that if we had the opportunity to end the game, we were going to try to end it," Cavs coach Hank Carter said.

On what was literally a win-or-go-home play, Lake Travis' gamble paid off.

Jason Carter hit a wide-open Smith in the back of the end zone to give the Cavs a 39-38 win over Cibolo Steele in a Class 6A Division I area-round playoff game at Rattler Stadium.

"We've been practicing that play for weeks now and we finally used it," Smith said. "In the huddle beforehand after they took the timeout, (offensive coordinator Tommy) Mangino was like, 'You ready to win this?' And I was like, 'I'm ready.'"

UIL overtime rules mirror NCAA rules, with each team starting its possession on the 25-yard line. Lake Travis won the extra-period coin toss and chose to be on defense.

Steele (9-2-1) quickly scored, and when Jason Carter - the head coach's son - ran onto the field, he knew the game would soon be over one way or another.

"Before the drive started, I asked my dad if we were going for two, and he said yes," Jason Carter said. "I loved it. I agreed with it. And we executed it just like I thought we would."

It took a monumental second-half effort by the Cavs just to force overtime.

Lake Travis trailed 28-14 at halftime and had allowed Knights running back Marshall Kenner to run for 219 yards and four touchdowns.

But the Cavs continued to excel on special teams (more on that later) clamped down on defense and did enough offensively to tie the game at 31-31.

Kenner, who ended with 301 yards rushing, scored his fifth TD to start overtime, then Lake Travis responded with Teddy Lofgren connecting with Luca Antoun for a 12-yard touchdown on a double pass.

"Steele was moving the ball. We were having a hard time tackling them. They were pushing us around, and we had two defensive starters out. The longer that thing went, I didn't think it was going to go great for us," Hank Carter said. "But I felt pretty good about going for it. We thought we were going to get a good look, and I was just kind of like, 'Here we go. This is our season.' And the kids got it done and we get to come back to work tomorrow."

With its offense struggling, Lake Travis' special teams and defense came up with big plays to keep it in the game.

Owen Aird's 53-yard interception return to the Steele 2-yard on the game's fifth play set up Lofgren's TD run the next play. And the Cavs' special teams produced or led to 17 points as Antoun returned a kickoff 92 yards for a touchdown, Nolan Atkins had a 65-yard kickoff return to the Knights 11 that led to another Lofgren rushing TD, and Hendrix Bryant recovered an onside kick that ultimately turned into a field goal.

The two teams met in the regular season but the game ended in a tie.

"I felt like the area that we needed to try to win by a wide margin was special teams," Hank Carter said. "Steele has a lot of dynamic players and is bigger than us. … We've been gradually getting better on special teams, and I thought if we were aggressive, we'd have some chances."

Though Antoun's kick return came in the first half, it was important as it came at a point when Steele had all the momentum and the Cavs' offense was struggling.

"I kind of slow-played it, found an opening, and the second that I saw the gap, I just shot it and was gone," Antoun said. "Special teams were a game changer tonight."

Lake Travis will play San Antonio Brennan in the regional semifinals Friday at Texas State. For Antoun and the Cavs, this playoff run has extra meaning.

"I love these guys, love these brothers," he said. "We've had the most adversity this year with our teammate ( Odin Hensley , who died before the season started), and so we know how to respond. We know how to fight back, and that's what we did tonight."

images.caption: The Lake Travis Cavaliers celebrate becoming Area Champions and advancing in the playoffs after beating Cibolo Steele in overtime at Rattler Stadium in San Marcos, Nov. 20, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman)

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka fuels breakup rumors after Lakers game appearance as engagement ring goes missing in LA
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka showed up at a Los Angeles Lakers game and on the red carpet at a YouTube Creator premiere this week.
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka showed up at a Los Angeles Lakers game and on the red carpet at a YouTube Creator premiere this week. Both times, her 12-carat engagement ring was missing from her hand. Online chatter about a breakup started almost right away. So far, no report backs that up. Sabalenka and fiancé Georgios Frangulis, a Brazilian entrepreneur, have not said the engagement is over. She stayed in California after the WTA Finals ended at Indian Wells last week, and she seems to be using the time to have some fun.Aryna Sabalenka seen without engagement ring in Los AngelesThe appearances came days after the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, where Mirra Andreeva beat Sabalenka. Instead of leaving, she stayed in California. Photos from the Lakers game and the YouTube event drew eyes for one reason: her bare hand.That stands out because she has been so open about the ring. Frangulis proposed on March 3, and Sabalenka wore the stone in matches at Indian Wells. She joked in an interview, "I requested 14 but I got 12."Some simple explanations are possible. A stone that size can be a security worry in a packed arena, and jewelry often stays home for a red carpet. One missing ring is thin evidence of anything.Rumors usually grow from small details like this one. A bare finger shows up in a photo, someone posts it, and a theory follows. I found no comment from either of them in the coverage so far.The couple's plans, as last reported, still stand. Sabalenka plans to marry after the 2027 US Open, though she admitted late this season that she had not started wedding planning. Nothing in that timeline suggests a split.Sabalenka ends the year at World No. 3On court, her season split in two. Sabalenka was unbeatable at the Sunshine Double of Indian Wells and Miami in March. The rest of the year was harder, and she finished third in the world rankings.Her year did have other highs. She won the Brisbane International in January, and in her trophy speech she told Frangulis, "Hopefully soon I can call you something else."That is a big change for a player who won at least one Grand Slam title in each year from 2023 to 2025. Staying on top is brutal work. Iga Swiatek went through the same thing before her, and the field eventually caught up with both.So some downtime in Los Angeles makes sense for a player who just finished a long year. A long season takes a toll, and tennis players rarely get long stretches to switch off.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Chaudhary helps Australia beat England in T20 shake-off of scandal-hit run
articles.summary: Australia beat England by three wickets with only one ball to spare as Nikhil Chaudhary’s 66 leads charge in Melbourne.
articles.body:
Nikhil Chaudhary blasted 66 and a late cameo from Jack Edwards helped Australia edge past England by three wickets with a ball to spare in the opening T20 International of the series.

Chaudhary’s 38-ball knock was crucial, but it was Edwards’ late flurry that got the job done, with the fast-bowler hitting an unbeaten 25 off 11 as they chased down a victory target of 188 on Saturday.

It ensured they took a 1-0 lead in the five-match series and temporarily lifted some of the clouds hanging over Australian cricket. Four of the country’s previous five matches have resulted in defeats, including a 2-1 One-Day International home series defeat by England.

The win also came on the day that Cricket Australia backed Pat Cummins to stay on as Test captain, despite continued allegations that he and the rest of the 2018 team were aware of the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball during their tour of South Africa.

England captain Harry Brook’s quickfire 65 had guided the visitors to 187-9 – the highest T20I score at the Melbourne Cricket Ground – but Australia’s response had already begun prior to the chase when their bowlers restricted the end of the tourists’ innings that had looked set to comfortably pass 200.

“Right, there is the future of the Australian cricket side with those young guys in it,” said Australia captain Mitchell Marsh.

“They’re a great bunch. Hopefully a win like that gives them a lot of confidence that they all belong.”

The run chase started badly for Australia with opener Jake Fraser-McGurk falling to just his third ball, undone by the spin of Liam Dawson.

Australia got going when debutant Sam Harper came in and took 20 off Jamie Overton’s first over.

But the 29-year-old swung the bat once too often and departed for 32 off 15 balls, earning new England fast-bowler Henry Crocombe a first T20 wicket.

They were 86-2 at the halfway mark, and when Dawson took a stunning catch to remove Marsh for 37, Australia’s hopes appeared to rest with Tim David.

But the big-hitter struggled to get going and was out for 20, leaving Chaudhary, in only his fourth T20 for Australia, in charge.

He departed chasing another boundary, only for Edwards to step up.

They needed 11 of the last over from Sam Curran, and when Edwards smacked a six off the first delivery, they were on their way to the win.

“Very entertaining to go down to the last couple of balls,” said Brook. “We were probably 10 runs short of what we needed on that surface.”

Earlier, England lost opener Phil Salt to the first ball and they were 13-2 in the third over after Aneurin Donald was also removed cheaply for 10.

But Brook went to town, smacking three straight sixes from paceman Riley Meredith.

He reached 50 off 20 deliveries before his fiery knock ended when he got a faint outside edge off Chaudhary to wicketkeeper Harper.

Tom Banton was put down on 11, among six dropped catches by Australia, but his luck ran out on 39 when another debutant, Lachlan Shaw, held on to a difficult chance.

The wickets kept tumbling with Curran caught out on 21 and Will Jacks out lbw for three, with Jordan Cox hitting 27 to keep the scoreboard moving.

articles.title: NHL Injury Update: Could Brendan Gallagher's injury during Vancouver Canucks' loss to Seattle Kraken threaten his NHL future
articles.summary: Brendan Gallagher suffers a serious injury during the Canucks' loss to the Kraken, raising concerns about his future in the NHL as he faces unrestricted free agency.
articles.body: Brendan Gallagher suffered a concerning lower-body injury during the Canucks' 5-1 loss to the Seattle Kraken Thursday night. The 34-year-old forward appeared to injure his left ankle or knee in a collision with a teammate in the second period.The Vancouver Canucks said Gallagher would not be returning with the injury. The incident throws into question his recovery timeline as the veteran heads into unrestricted free agency and an uncertain future in the NHL.What Brendan Gallagher's injury means for Vancouver CanucksBrendan Gallagher’s injury is just another headache for the Vancouver Canucks, who are already having a tough season. The team announced a lower-body injury for the veteran forward, who left the game after just 3:02 of ice time.It happened in the second period against the Seattle Kraken. Gallagher went down awkwardly close to the opposition’s net after contact with a teammate. He left the ice looking like he was in a lot of pain and headed for the locker room.What happened to Brendan Gallagher against Seattle Kraken?It was a rough night for Vancouver, and Gallagher’s injury was the final blow in a 5-1 loss. It is still not clear exactly what and how bad the injury is, but the initial worry was his left ankle or knee.Gallagher would not return to the contest, the Canucks said. But a detailed medical diagnosis and a timetable for recovery were not immediately available.How has Brendan Gallagher performed for Vancouver Canucks?Gallagher was acquired by the Vancouver Canucks in the summer in a deal that also included future considerations. But since he made the move to the team, he hasn’t put up the offensive numbers of a veteran NHL forward.Gallagher had three assists in 21 games during the 2026-27 season without a goal. His offensive production has waned as Vancouver has struggled near the bottom of the league standings.The veteran winger proved to be a hardworking and competitive forward during his long stint with the Montreal Canadiens. His career stats are 246 goals and 244 assists in 932 regular-season games.Could Brendan Gallagher's injury affect his NHL future?Gallagher’s injury comes at a particularly important time in his career. The 34-year-old is in the final year of a six-year, $39 million deal and is nearing unrestricted free agency.The injury could complicate his immediate playing situation depending on the severity and recovery. But there’s no confirmed sign at this point that the incident will be the end of his NHL career.His experience, physical style of play, and history of playing through injuries are still big parts of his professional profile. A medical update from Vancouver will give a better idea of how soon he can return.The Vancouver Canucks are set to play the Minnesota Wild on Saturday. Gallagher’s status for that game will be determined after further medical evaluation, and the team is hoping to hear some good news about its veteran forward.Note: The injury's exact diagnosis, recovery period, and any career-ending implications remain unconfirmed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Man City claw back 1-1 draw with Fulham to end three-game losing streak
articles.summary: Rodrigo Muniz set Fulham on the way but Elliot Anderson volley earns Manchester City a valuable Premier League point.
articles.body:
Manchester City avoided the ignominy of a fourth-straight defeat as Elliot Anderson’s strike kept an unsettled Etihad Stadium at bay in a 1-1 draw with Fulham in the Premier League.

Rodrigo Muniz opened the scoring in the 16th minute for the away side, who had only won two of their opening 10 league games to start the day just two points and three places above the relegation zone.

Anderson’s driven volley from the edge of the box in the 57th minute handed City their first point in the league since they opened their campaign with seven consecutive wins.

The midfielder, who had netted his first City goal since arriving from Nottingham Forest, nearly added a second with a burst into the box, but dragged his effort across the face.

City, who sit five points off top spot, had lost to Brighton, RB Leipzig and Forest in their previous games.

Holders and league leaders Arsenal play their game in hand over City at Newcastle later on Saturday.

City held one of the longest winning streaks in English football history with 20 straight victories over Fulham dating back to 2012.

That run is now over, but City’s run of poor results is not.

Boos from the home support greeted the final whistle, with City’s winless run in the league extending to four games — a stretch that has come soon after the club was found guilty of large-scale financial rule-breaking that leaves its future shrouded in uncertainty.

The display was far from convincing for City, with Erling Haaland guilty of wasting two great chances in the first half — and having one goal ruled out in contentious circumstances.

After having a close-range effort saved by Bernd Leno, Haaland followed up and bundled the ball out of the Fulham goalkeeper’s possession and into the net on the goal line.

It was judged that Haaland kicked the ball out of Leno’s hands, with the Premier League saying Leno was deemed to be “in control of the ball”.

articles.title: The Rock Slams Pat McAfee Through a Table in Viral Video of WWE, Miami Icon on ESPN College GameDay
articles.summary: Ahead of his upcoming appearance at Survivor Series next weekend, WWE legend Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson showed Saturday on ESPN College GameDay that he's still in prime fighting shape.
articles.body:
Ahead of his upcoming appearance at Survivor Series next weekend, WWE legend Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson showed Saturday on ESPN College GameDay that he's still in prime fighting shape.

With College GameDay on location at his alma mater, the University of Miami, The Rock was in attendance, and he made his presence felt by hitting host Pat McAfee with a Rock Bottom through a table.

During his College GameDay appearance, The Rock was wearing the No. 94 jersey he wore during his time as a defensive lineman for the Hurricanes.

The Rock Bottom came just days after The Rock announced on the Pat McAfee Show that he would be on hand for Survivor Series in Houston on Nov. 28 to celebrate the 30-year anniversary of his WWE debut at Survivor Series 1996.

Despite the fact that The Rock is now 54 years of age and hasn't wrestled a match in nearly three years, he looked to be in great shape on Saturday, which should only serve to fuel rumors and speculation of an in-ring return.

articles.title: Liverpool vs Manchester United: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
articles.summary: One of sport’s biggest rivalries takes centre stage as Liverpool host a Man United side in the EPL relegation zone.
articles.body:
Who: Liverpool vs Manchester United What: English Premier League When: Sunday, November 22 , at 4:30pm (16:30 GMT) Where: Anfield in Liverpool, United Kingdom How to follow: Al Jazeera will have full text commentary coverage of the game with build-up from 13:30 GMT

The latest rebuild of Manchester United begins at Liverpool on Sunday with Mauricio Pochettino in the hot seat – a position that some see as the impossible job.

The match at Anfield comes four days after the arrival of the Argentinian , who only oversaw his final game as United States coach on Wednesday.

The 54-year-old is tasked with ending a 13-year wait for a 21st Premier League title – only Liverpool have won the competition as many times as the Red Devils.

United sacked Michael Carrick last week with the team third from bottom in the league and suffering their worst league start for 40 years.

Pochettino is the ninth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired with the club’s last league title in 2014 and he is the fourth in the last three years.

United’s recent pain is made worse by Liverpool’s revival in the last decade, with the Reds sitting fourth in the table and hoping to mount a challenge this season to move clear as the team with the most English top-flight titles.

What were the key takeaways from Pochettino’s Man United media conference?

Given the swift turnaround from his previous role to his new one, Pochettino’s unveiling as United manager was combined with the pre-game media briefing ahead of the Anfield trip.

Understandably, most of the questions centred on how United’s form can be reversed in the short and long-term.

“It is about building our own way here,” Pochettino said when asked what he can do differently to the other managers who have taken on the role since Ferguson’s farewell. “The past is not going to help, to think about yesterday.”

“We feel the support and we are going to work really hard to help the players to perform. That is the priority.

“It is normal when you don’t win games that the confidence starts to go down,” he said. “I think the players need to feel from us that we believe and trust in them.

“With the schedule we have ahead we have to settle on our principles. The players are intelligent, they have quality. Sometimes it is unlocking some things that didn’t appear for different reasons.”

A key figure ⁠⁠⁠⁠in any rebuilding effort will be captain Bruno Fernandes, whose future has been the subject of speculation as he has ⁠⁠⁠⁠yet to agree a new deal.

Pochettino revealed he had already held extensive talks with the Portugal midfielder and indicated he remained central to his plans.

“Bruno is our captain and a very important player but other players have to feel they are important from the bottom to the top,” he said.

“We spoke, I spent three hours chatting with all the players individually. It was ⁠⁠⁠⁠very nice contact.”

Questions about the squad’s fitness levels have swirled around Old Trafford, but Pochettino refused to criticise what he had inherited.

“It is about proposing that idea to be brave and take it to the field,” he said.

“We ⁠⁠⁠⁠cannot talk about data without context. It is easy to manipulate data but we need to ⁠⁠⁠⁠be honest, sometimes they don’t show something that you can see on the field.

“We are here not to denounce things. We are here to build something with our players.”

Liverpool had lost consecutive games before their 3-1 win against bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace in their last match.

The run summed up the mixed start to life at Anfield for Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the summer – the former Bournemouth manager admits an epic encounter awaits.

“You don’t find bigger games than this, honestly. I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be part of these games,” Iraola said.

“We have to acknowledge the importance of the game, and also a lot of ingredients, such as their new manager.

“It is important for us in lots of different ways because we want to improve our form at home and the first chance we have to do that is on Sunday.”

Iraola also admitted he fears Pochettino, whose Premier League experience was gained at Tottenham and Chelsea, will have an advantage because he does not know the Argentinian’s preferred tactics with his new club.

“We’ve faced each other. Obviously he has a lot of Premier League games that we can look at and we can look at games in the US, but they still have this small advantage,” Iraola said.

“We don’t have references to prepare because they can go different ways that we don’t actually know.

“The staff have been working with them, so they are going to arrive well prepared. We don’t have the references that we have against other teams.”

Iraola will have to adapt on the fly and the Spaniard plans to switch up his game plan if he is caught out by Pochettino’s tactics.

“Especially the beginning of the game will be important as we have to adapt to certain things and manage the situation as quick as possible,” he said.

“Every time there is a new manager you want to impress. It happens everywhere. But we have been focusing more on us, how we can improve.”

What happened the last time Liverpool played Man United?

United were 3-2 winners when the sides met in the Premier League at Old Trafford last season.

Liverpool fought back from two goals down in May, only for Kobbie Mainoo to net the late winner from the edge of the box.

What happened in the corresponding fixture last season?

United were 2-1 winners at Anfield in October last year, with Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire scoring either side of Cody Gakpo’s strike.

When did Liverpool last beat Manchester United?

Liverpool last beat United with a 3-0 win at Old Trafford in the Premier League in September 2024.

Luis Diaz scored twice and Mohamed Salah netted the other in the win for Arne Slot’s side.

When did Liverpool last beat Manchester United at Anfield?

Remarkably, the Reds haven’t beaten their fierce rivals at home since Jurgen Klopp’s side emerged victorious in March 2023.

The result on that occasion was, however, an emphatic 7-0 win for Cody Gakpo, Darwin Nunez and Mohamed Salah all scoring twice, before Roberto Firmino added the seventh.

The two following seasons in the matchup at Anfield resulted in draws.

Liverpool have been given a 57.3 percent chance of winning the game by Opta’s supercomputer, while United have only been given a 29.5 percent chance of claiming the spoils.

This will be their 219th meeting, with United winning 85 of the encounters and Liverpool 72.

The fixture dates back to a 2-1 win for Liverpool in April 1894.

Liverpool are boosted by the return of injured trio Jeremie Frimpong, Ryan Gravenberch and Virgil van Dijk, while Dominik Szoboszlai has also been cleared to play.

Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley have returned to training but are ⁠⁠⁠⁠not yet available. Hugo Ekitike is still sidelined.

Alisson; Araujo, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Gakpo, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak

Patrick Dorgu and Harry Maguire are back in training after knocks, while Lisandro Martinez returns from suspension.

Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford are closing in on comebacks from knocks, but it is thought that the Liverpool match will come too soon.

Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko remain out.

Predicted Manchester United starting lineup
