articles.title: College Football Playoff: Which Big Ten Bubble Team Could Make the Most Noise?
articles.summary: Which Big Ten team on the College Football Playoff bubble is the most dangerous: Oregon, Ohio State or Iowa?
articles.body: Only two Big Ten teams are currently in the updated College Football Playoff field (No. 4 UCLA and No. 8 Indiana), but could another program break through? Tuesday's rankings reveal featured three Big Ten teams in the 13-15 spots: Oregon, Ohio State and Iowa. Both the Ducks (8-3) and Buckeyes (7-3) have three losses, while the Hawkeyes are 8-2 and seeking their first-ever College Football Playoff berth. So, which of these three teams could wreak havoc in the playoff if it wins out and gets some help from elsewhere? Mark Ingram, Urban Meyer and Chris "The Bear" Fallica made their case for the most dangerous Big Ten team of the aforementioned bunch on Week 12's edition of "Big Noon Kickoff." Mark Ingram: Oregon What Ingram Said: "This is the team that we expected from the start of the season. Ever since Jay Johnson took over the playcalling, this offense has been explosive and dynamic. [Quarterback] Dylan Raiola is playing confidently and pushing the ball downfield. But then, defensively, this team has been dominant the last three-to-four games during this win streak. So, you talk about Oregon and getting the best 12 teams into the playoff, Oregon looks like they're certainly that right now." Oregon Context: The Ducks have won four consecutive games, including beating the Buckeyes on the road (41-28) and winning their last two games over Michigan and Michigan State by a combined score of 76-14. Over Oregon's last four games, Raiola has totaled 1,168 passing yards, 10 passing touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 164.7 passer rating, while completing 66.2% of his passes. Urban Meyer: Ohio State What Meyer Said: "Ohio State, obviously, they can't jump Oregon, and they won't jump Oregon. But you better be careful not to keep penalizing these teams that play the real games out of conference. Ohio State went to Texas, lost in the final seconds, and they're going to be penalized. If they would've played Akron and beat them by 50 points, they'd be in the playoff. Last year, Texas went to Ohio State, lost in the final seconds of the game, and they got kept out. "You think last year's schedules were bad in the non-conference? Wait until what's going to start happening. You're going to see mercy rules in college football. To me, a loss to Texas at Texas is better than a win by 55 points against Akron. Somehow, you have to do that." Ohio State Context: Each of Ohio State's three losses have come against ranked teams (Texas, USC and Oregon). Following consecutive losses to USC and Oregon, Ohio State beat Northwestern at home last week. The Buckeyes are without starting quarterback Julian Sayin, who suffered an elbow injury in the team's Oct. 17 win over Indiana and is expected to miss the rest of the regular season. The Bear: Oregon What "The Bear" Said: "I think they've simplified things for Dylan Raiola. They've made it quick, don't think, just get the ball out to all those wide receivers. If you look at their résumé, as a whole, only three teams have five wins over top-40 teams: Texas, Georgia and Oregon. Now, they have the bad losses, but you can kind of say one was seven turnovers against UCLA, you played a Power Four team on the road in the non-conference, and then you had every wide receiver out for the Illinois game. "I think the committee told you this week by moving them to No. 13 that they are very much in the mix. The Oregon team we see now, I think, is the Oregon team that the committee is judging them on because they've shown they can do it with a new coordinator and Raiola." More Oregon Context: Oregon's last game of the regular season is a home matchup against Washington (6-4) on Nov. 28.

articles.title: Samuel Martínez rescata a Colombia en el final ante Japón en el Mundial Sub-17
articles.standfirst: Colombia vs. Japón (2-1): resultado, goles y debut en el Mundial Sub-17 2026
articles.summary: Colombia vs. Japón (2-1): resultado, goles y debut en el Mundial Sub-17 2026
articles.body: La Selección Colombia Sub-17 inició con el pie derecho su participación en la Copa Mundial de Catar 2026 al imponerse 2-1 sobre Japón en un encuentro vibrante, disputado y definido en el tiempo de reposición en Rayán / Doha. El vigente campeón sudamericano de la categoría sufrió ante el empuje del campeón asiático, pero encontró en el talento y la sangre fría del canterano de Atlético Nacional Samuel Martínez el golpe definitivo para quedarse con los primeros tres puntos del Grupo L. El conjunto dirigido por Freddy Hurtado no tardó en golpear el marcador pese a que el trámite del juego exigía paciencia. Apenas en los primeros compases del partido (alrededor del minuto 5, tras una acción gestada por el costado derecho), Miguel Ágamez, atacante formado en las divisiones menores del Junior de Barranquilla, capitalizó una jugada ofensiva pisando el área con decisión y definiendo con potencia para firmar el 1-0. El tanto ratificó el olfato goleador que ya había mostrado en el Sudamericano de Paraguay. Sin embargo, el cuadro japonés, comandado por Shinji Ono, asumió el control territorial y la posesión del balón durante buena parte de la primera etapa. Con movilidad y asociaciones rápidas, los nipones generaron aproximaciones y pusieron a prueba el orden defensivo de la Tricolor, que incluso se salvó de un susto mayor cuando una acción de gol asiática fue invalidada por fuera de juego. El empate llegó al minuto 38: tras una desatención en las marcas dentro del área colombiana, Kakeru Saito conectó de frente para decretar el 1-1 con el que ambos equipos se marcharon al descanso, dejando abierta la historia para el complemento. En la segunda mitad, el guion mantuvo la tensión y la paridad táctica hasta que los movimientos desde los bancos comenzaron a inclinar la balanza. Freddy Hurtado apostó por refrescar bandas y circulación —con variantes como el ingreso de Jhon Moreno para dar profundidad por derecha y posteriormente Simón Rojas para ganar control y criterio en el mediocampo—, mientras que Shinji Ono movió piezas buscando romper el bloque rival. El punto de inflexión llegó en el tramo final. Samuel Martínez, el '10' surgido de la cantera de Guarne en Atlético Nacional y una de las grandes promesas del fútbol colombiano (con proyección hacia el Liverpool al cumplir la mayoría de edad), ingresó desde el banquillo alrededor del minuto 76 para cambiarle la cara al ataque tricolor. A los 80 minutos, el partido dio un giro clave cuando el árbitro francés Willy Delajod expulsó por doble amonestación al capitán y defensor japonés Anthony Motosuna tras una infracción sobre Martínez, decisión que se sostuvo tras revisión de video. Con superioridad numérica, Colombia adelantó líneas y cercó el arco rival. Cuando el reloj avanzaba hacia el final del tiempo reglamentario (alrededor del minuto 89), Samuel Martínez controló al borde del área, encaró a su marca y cayó dentro del área tras el contacto de Hoshi. Delajod sancionó penalti y, pese al reclamo y la revisión tecnológica solicitada por el conjunto nipón, la pena máxima se mantuvo. Ya en el tiempo añadido (90+3', registrado oficialmente en el minuto 92:48), Martínez asumió la responsabilidad desde los doce pasos y definió con serenidad y precisión para el 2-1 definitivo. Según destacó la Conmebol, ese tanto se convirtió en el gol más tardío de la Selección Colombia en la historia de la Copa Mundial de la FIFA de la categoría. Más allá de las dificultades atravesadas —especialmente en los tramos en que Japón impuso su posesión y obligó a resistir en campo propio—, el estreno dejó un balance altamente positivo: carácter competitivo, impacto inmediato desde el banco y liderazgo provisional en el Grupo L. La Selección Colombia Sub-17 volverá a la acción el martes 24 de noviembre de 2026 a las 10:30 a. m. (hora de Colombia) frente a Honduras, y cerrará la fase de grupos el viernes 27 de noviembre ante Serbia, ambos compromisos en territorio catarí.

articles.title: Bogotá declara Alerta Fase 1 por contaminación del aire en cuatro zonas de la ciudad: restricciones vigentes y qué tener en cuenta
articles.standfirst: Alerta por contaminación del aire en el suroccidente de Bogotá: restricciones y recomendaciones
articles.summary: Alerta por contaminación del aire en el suroccidente de Bogotá: restricciones y recomendaciones
articles.body: La Alcaldía Mayor de Bogotá, a través de la Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (SDA), declaró este sábado 21 de noviembre de 2026 la Alerta Fase 1 por contaminación del aire en cuatro sectores clave del suroccidente de la ciudad: Kennedy, Arborizadora, Puente Aranda y Patio Bonito. La medida preventiva se activó luego de que las estaciones de monitoreo de calidad del aire Carvajal-Sevillana, Ciudad Bolívar, Puente Aranda y Kennedy registraran niveles regulares durante 36 horas consecutivas, impulsados principalmente por el aumento de material particulado PM10. El deterioro del aire en el suroccidente bogotano responde a una combinación de emisiones locales y condiciones meteorológicas adversas que impiden que los contaminantes se dispersen con normalidad: Incremento de partículas PM10: Estas partículas suspendidas provienen del polvo resuspendido por el tránsito vehicular, las obras de construcción, las actividades industriales y el humo de incendios. Condiciones climáticas desfavorables: Los vientos débiles reducen la ventilación natural y las bajas temperaturas de la madrugada favorecen la acumulación de contaminantes cerca de la superficie. Influencia de incendios externos: El análisis técnico de las autoridades ambientales identificó una posible influencia del humo proveniente de incendios en Venezuela, la Orinoquía y la Amazonía, sumándose a las fuentes de emisión de la ciudad. La alerta se mantendrá activa hasta que las estaciones de monitoreo registren niveles bajos o moderados durante 36 horas continuas, de acuerdo con el seguimiento técnico de la Secretaría de Ambiente. Para frenar la acumulación de contaminantes y proteger a la población, el Distrito puso en marcha controles reforzados y restricciones temporales dirigidas principalmente a la industria y al transporte: Industria (calderas y equipos): Restricción de operación de calderas y equipos con combustibles sólidos o líquidos desde este sábado entre las 6:00 a. m. y las 3:00 p. m. (con posibilidad de extenderse de lunes a sábado en ese mismo horario la próxima semana). Combustibles de respaldo: Prohibición de cambiar a combustibles sólidos o líquidos de respaldo en equipos que puedan operar con otras fuentes (por ejemplo, una caldera de gas no puede pasar a diésel o carbón). Sistemas de control: Obligación de mantener activos los sistemas de control de emisiones y suspender mantenimientos que impliquen detenerlos temporalmente. Movilidad y vigilancia: Refuerzo del monitoreo ambiental, mayores controles a establecimientos industriales y operativos en vía dirigidos a vehículos. La Secretaría de Salud y las autoridades distritales hicieron un llamado a residentes, trabajadores y visitantes de las zonas cubiertas —y a la ciudadanía en general— para reducir la exposición a partículas contaminantes, poniendo especial atención en niños y niñas, personas mayores, mujeres gestantes y personas con enfermedades crónicas: Consultar el IBOCA: Revisar periódicamente el Índice Bogotano de Calidad del Aire y Riesgo en Salud (IBOCA) antes de planear actividades al aire libre. Evitar ejercicio intenso al aire libre: Reducir o suspender la actividad física vigorosa en espacios abiertos, especialmente en los grupos de mayor vulnerabilidad. Cuidar el aire en casa: Evitar fumar tabaco o usar cigarrillos electrónicos, encender velas, incienso o estufas de leña dentro de la vivienda. Limpieza sin levantar polvo: Preferir trapos húmedos para la limpieza y evitar barrer en seco. Atención a señales de alarma: Acudir a un servicio de urgencias ante dificultad para respirar, dolor en el pecho, fiebre persistente o fatiga inusual. En bebés y niños pequeños, vigilar respiración rápida, hundimiento de las costillas al respirar o rechazo del alimento. También está habilitada la línea 137 para orientación en salud y la línea 195 para información distrital.

articles.title: 'Big Noon Kickoff' Crew Predict Conference Championship Matchups And Winners
articles.summary: The "Big Noon Kickoff" crew gave their predictions for who will appear in and win the Big Ten, SEC, Big 12 and ACC championship games.
articles.body: A familiar face on top in the Big Ten. Revenge in the SEC. A first-time playoff berth in the Big 12. A stunner in the ACC. FOX Sports' Urban Meyer, Chris "The Bear" Fallica, Brady Quinn and Matt Leinart gave their picks to win the Power Four conference championship games on "Big Noon Kickoff." Meyer: Indiana Over UCLA What Urban Meyer Said: "Both of them [Indiana and UCLA] control their own destiny. Here's the beautiful thing about that title game in Indianapolis: It will be big-boy football. Strength versus strength. Indiana has one of the top defenses in America, and UCLA has one of the great offensive lines in college football. Indiana defensive coordinator Bryant Haines, I think he's one of the best in the business and should be a head coach pretty soon. I pick Indiana in a tight one because of the defense of Indiana." Indiana Context: The defending national champions currently sit at 9-1 and are the No. 8-ranked team in the nation. Indiana recently made a quarterback change, going from Josh Hoover to Grant Wilson. The Hoosiers have one ranked win this season, which came last weekend against USC. The Bear: Texas Over Georgia What Chris "The Bear" Fallica Said: "The Texas defense has been fantastic all year long. Yes, they have blown a couple of big leads and have some upset losses. However, Will Muschamp getting an opportunity to beat Georgia in the SEC championship game? Maybe Arch Manning and that offense can finally put it together? Give me the Longhorns for an upset." Texas Context: The No. 5-ranked Longhorns have two losses, but they also have ranked victories over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri and – at the time of the game – LSU. Texas overcame an 11-point second half deficit to get the road win over LSU, as Manning hit running back Raleek Brown for a go-ahead, 4-yard touchdown with three seconds remaining in the game. Texas has lost each of its last three contests against Georgia dating back to the 2024 season. Quinn: Utah Over Texas Tech What Brady Quinn Said: "Those two teams, to me, are the best in the Big 12. They've separated themselves, in particular Texas Tech, since they've moved to Tommy Castellanos at quarterback. … He's added another portion of this offense that they really didn't have before to take off and run with the football. "And then, Utah, [quarterback] Devon Dampier is just a winner. Bottom line, it doesn't matter what position you put him in. He can play running back and run it in. He'll play quarterback, take off, make a play with his legs. This defense is stingy. I think when it's all said and done, Utah ends up winning the Big 12. You just can't bet against Devon Dampier. This young man deserves a lot more credit, and he should be in New York City for the Heisman Trophy." Utah Context: The No. 2-ranked Utes are one of just two undefeated teams in the current College Football Playoff field and have three ranked wins under their belt against Houston, BYU and Arizona. Dampier has totaled 2,257 passing yards, 22 passing touchdowns, eight interceptions and a 155.1 passer rating, while completing 66.5% of his passes. He has also rushed for 582 yards and nine touchdowns. Leinart: Wake Forest Over Miami What Matt Leinart Said: "I think Wake Forest is the most dangerous team in all of college football right now. We know a lot about the offense. I think [Wake Forest quarterback] Gio Lopez should join Devon Dampier in New York City in a couple of weeks. … This is one of the best passing offenses in the country. They're electric, and we know, with Miami, a concern is its defense, but for me, with Wake Forest, it's their defense that stands out. Since Week 5, they have the No. 1 scoring defense in the country. I know one of those teams was Merrimack, but they're beating up conference opponents. Over the last six games, they've outscored teams 313-38. They are a machine right now." Wake Forest Context: The No. 11-ranked Demon Deacons are 9-1 overall, with their only loss coming at home against the No. 7-ranked Miami Hurricanes. Lopez has totaled 2,377 passing yards, 19 passing touchdowns, one interception and a 168.9 passer rating through nine games, while completing 66.0% of his passes. He has also rushed for 351 yards and eight touchdowns.

articles.title: 'I'll Cut Off My Right Arm': Inside Jim Harbaugh's Obsession With Beating Ohio State
articles.summary: There weren't many things former Michigan quarterback and head coach Jim Harbaugh valued more than beating Ohio State.
articles.body: There weren't many things former Michigan quarterback and head coach Jim Harbaugh valued more than beating Ohio State. If anyone needed a reminder of just how seriously he took the rivalry, one team meeting made that abundantly clear. "We're in this meeting, and he said, 'I'll cut off my right arm to beat Ohio State,'" former Michigan running back Blake Corum recalled in a first-look teaser for FOX Sports' upcoming two-part documentary, "The Team: Michigan Football." "Some guys might have chuckled or laughed, but the look in his eyes, he wasn't smirking, he wasn't laughing, he was dead serious." The short teaser, which was released during Saturday's airing of "Big Noon Kickoff," features footage of Harbaugh addressing the media. "Beat Ohio. We're gonna do it or die trying," Harbaugh declares. The preview then takes viewers through the history of "The Game," showcasing some of the rivalry's most memorable moments, from coaching showdowns between Woody Hayes and Bo Schembechler to the more recent chapters featuring Harbaugh and Ohio State head coach Ryan Day. The clip closes with one final reminder of how much this rivalry means to the Wolverines: "There's one thing we need to do. Prepare so we can beat Ohio State." Executive produced by Harbaugh and former Michigan quarterback Tom Brady, "The Team: Michigan Football" will offer a deeper look at the program's history and legacy. Part 1 premieres Friday, Nov. 27, at 7 p.m. ET on FOX, the night before Michigan and Ohio State meet in "The Game" on "Big Noon Saturday." Part 2 will air Saturday, Dec. 12, at 6:30 p.m. ET. articles.title: Noni Madueke salvages draw for Arsenal at Newcastle United as Raya injured
articles.summary: League leaders Arsenal miss the chance to go eight points clear of second placed Brighton, who play on Sunday.
articles.body:
Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw .

The Gunners led on Saturday through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes.

But Mikel Arteta’s men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle.

Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points.

However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise.

Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions.

Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second-half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St James’ Park.

Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title.

Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on.

Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a 75 million pound ($98m) move to the Emirates Stadium in August.

The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener.

It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek.

Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break.

Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so.

Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level.

Suddenly, an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks.

Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya.

That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell.

But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title.

Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the righ,t and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek.

Madueke told Sky Sports that he thought 2-2 was a “fair” result.

“Game of two halves is fair. First half we were outstanding. Should have got three goals, to be honest. Missed a couple of chances myself. Everything else was there,” he said.

“The second half, the first 20 minutes, was not good by our standard. When you give this team and crowd belief at home, it is difficult. We showed character to get back in the game, but 2-2 is a fair result.”

articles.title: Steelers activate WR Roman Wilson ahead of Eagles matchup
articles.summary: Pittsburgh makes a flurry of roster moves ahead of Week 11.
articles.body:
The Steelers are getting one of their top wide receivers back ahead of Week 11's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Pittsburgh announced Saturday that wide receiver Roman Wilson has been activated to the 53-man roster ahead of Sunday's game. In addition, the team announced the signing of edge rusher K.J. Henry from the practice squad to the roster. The two signings fill the open spots on the Steelers' roster.

The Henry signing follows the Steelers announcing outside linebacker Nick Herbig as out for Sunday's game. Now, Pittsburgh has an open slot on its practice squad.

Besides adding Wilson and Henry to the roster, the Steelers also announced that wide receiver Max Hurleman and offensive lineman Doug Nester have been elevated from the practice squad to the active/inactive roster ahead of the Eagles game. Both will revert back to the practice squad following the game.

Both Wilson and Hurleman were recently on injured reserve for the Steelers. Wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. and offensive lineman Gennings Dunker remain on IR but in their 21-day return windows.

articles.summary: Steelers WR Roman Wilson will be available for Week 11 after being activated off Injured Reserve
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers WR Roman Wilson (hand) was activated from the Reserve/Injured list Saturday, Nov. 21.

articles.title: What Detroit Mercy HC Mark Montgomery said about MSU in his return

articles.body:

The game featured Tom Izzo going up against one of his former assistant coaches, Mark Montgomery, who is in his third season leading the Titans program.

After the game, Montgomery spoke to the media where he talked about Michigan State and shared his thoughts on the Spartans team and the opportunity he got to play against his former boss.

"When Michigan State is clicking at all cylinders, they are going to be tough to beat."

"I was here when we recruited Kur Teng. I jokingly told my guys at half he hadn't hit the shot in a year. I helped recruit Fears, he didn't have to put 17 AND 14 on me."

"You know Michigan State has another gear they can go to."

"We could've just switched play sheets, play calls. We have lots of similarities. When you watch them (MSU) on film, that is what you want to look like. This is what fast break, cutouts, look like."

"Recruits want to play in games like this, we want to coach in games like this," mentions wanting to play the Spartans every year. "We know what we have to do in conference play."

"I'm through and through green-and-white when I'm not playing them, I watched the game against Oregon (last night). My GAs were letting me know the score (against Duke)."

articles.title: Michigan Suspends WR Andrew Marsh Following Criminal Charge
articles.summary: Michigan has suspended wide receiver Andrew Marsh for Saturday's UCLA game following news of a misdemeanor indecent exposure charge.
articles.body:
The Michigan Wolverines have officially suspended wide receiver Andrew Marsh for Saturday's game against No. 4 UCLA, and the decision comes just days after news broke that the sophomore is facing a misdemeanor indecent exposure charge.

According to ESPN's Adam Rittenberg , Michigan confirmed Saturday afternoon that Marsh has been suspended for the game. The announcement provides important clarification after Marsh was listed as OUT on the Big Ten's final availability report earlier in the day.

"Marsh has been suspended for today's game, per the team." — Adam Rittenberg, ESPN

Michigan Confirms Andrew Marsh Suspension

Marsh had been listed as questionable throughout the week as Michigan prepared for its final home game of the 2026 season. However, following the emergence of his legal situation, questions surfaced about whether he would be permitted to play against the Bruins.

According to previous reporting from the Associated Press , Marsh is facing a misdemeanor charge stemming from an alleged incident involving a food delivery driver earlier this year. The allegations have not been proven in court, and Marsh is presumed innocent.

Michigan previously released a statement addressing the situation , but the program had not publicly confirmed a suspension at that time. Rittenberg's latest report now establishes that Marsh's absence against UCLA is the result of a team-issued suspension.

The university has not announced whether additional disciplinary action will follow.

Michigan Loses Key Offensive Weapon Against UCLA

The suspension creates another problem for head coach Kyle Whittingham, whose team enters Saturday's matchup with a 5-5 record. Marsh has been one of Michigan's most productive receivers this season, recording 48 receptions for 459 yards and one touchdown.

The Wolverines are already dealing with significant injury problems heading into the UCLA game . Wide receivers JJ Buchanan, Jaylen Pile, and Braydon Alford are also unavailable, leaving Michigan particularly thin at the position.

Saturday's suspension is the latest development in a difficult week for Marsh and the Wolverines. With Michigan fighting for bowl eligibility against undefeated UCLA, the timing certainly couldn't be much worse.

For now, Marsh will not play against UCLA, and Michigan has not publicly announced when he will be eligible to return.

articles.title: ‘Zero percent of me agrees with this’: Sophie Cunningham reacts after coach is suspended for pushing player in head
articles.summary: Iowa State Cyclones women’s basketball head coach Bill Fennelly was suspended for pushing guard Sienna Harvey’s head during a timeout with two minutes remain...
articles.body:
Iowa State Cyclones women's basketball head coach Bill Fennelly was suspended for pushing guard Sienna Harvey's head during a timeout with two minutes remaining in the Cyclones' Sunday win over UIC.

"We cannot tolerate inappropriate contact between a coach or staff member and a student-athlete in practice or in competition, whether intentional or not," Iowa State athletic director Jared Benko said in a statement. "We have high expectations of all of our coaches, staff and student-athletes and we will not shy away from holding accountable those who fail to meet those expectations. I have met with Coach Fennelly and he has apologized to the student-athlete involved and regrets his actions."

However, Harvey defended her coach during the week.

"Obviously all of us like to be coached hard. We all have a great relationship with our coach," Harvey said on Wednesday . "I can see how it was perceived on the internet. But he loves us and cares about us more than anyone … And I like being coached hard … It was just perceived differently to what it was."

Now, WNBA free agent Sophie Cunningham is weighing in.

"I don't agree with it," Cunningham said of the suspension on her podcast No Hesitation. "I don't agree with it. I did not think anything was wrong with it. I think that she maybe made a mistake, or she wasn't dialed in.

"That's okay. Like, he's gonna get on her. And I think that was him like, hey, get your head together. Like, we need you. Like, people were taking that as like a physical like he pushed her type thing. Maybe that's our generation. I think this is soft. I, I don't, I don't like that he got suspended for this at all. Like, zero percent of me agrees with this."

Her co-host, Drew Hanlen, agreed, but with the caveat that it's never acceptable for a mant ot put hands on a woman.

"I know, and I love that. And that's why I love you," Cunningham responded. "And I like— you respect us, we respect you, because that's the type of man you are. But I am telling you… It's just a part of competing together at a high level. And I just, I love my male coaches."

As much as Cunningham may welcome the tough coaching, times are changing, and Fennelly, who is in his 32nd season leading the program, seems well aware of that, announcing even before the incident that he intends to retire after this season.

articles.title: ‘Boring’ Los Angeles Lakers Forward Highlighted for Having Brilliant Season
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers sit atop the Western Conference standings following a 106-104 win over the Sacramento Kings on Friday. The Lakers improved to 14-3 as...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers sit atop the Western Conference standings following a 106-104 win over the Sacramento Kings on Friday.

The Lakers improved to 14-3 as Luka Doncic continued his MVP campaign. Doncic is averaging 37.2 points, 6.8 rebounds, 7.7 assists and 1.9 steals.

While Doncic is carrying the load offensively, the Lakers' defense is being held together by players like Walker Kessler, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams.

Lakers Forward Called 'Boring' and 'Brilliant'

GettyMatisse Thybulle #4 of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the first half of a game against the LA Clippers at Intuit Dome on October 28, 2026 in Inglewood, California.

On a recent episode of The Bill Simmons Podcast , The Ringer founder highlighted the season Matisse Thybulle is having as one of the best glue guys in the league.

"Let's go ahead and give at least one brilliantly boring glue guy the spotlight they deserve," Simmons said via ClutchPoints . "When you have somebody as great as Luka offensively, you can afford to have the one role guy who's just, 'I'm just here to play awesome defense and make hustle plays and fill in the blanks.' And he's finally found his stride all these years later."

"I held onto my Thybulle stock," he added. "It wasn't worth a lot. There wasn't a reason to sell it because it was going for nothing. … It's been nice to see him finally used correctly."

In 17 games this season, Thybulle is averaging 7.5 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 2.3 steals. He has flourished as one of the starting forwards as a key 3-and-D player. He is knocking down 40.5 percent of his 3-point shots and is second in the league in steals per game.

The Lakers signed Thybulle to a one-year, $3.3 million deal in the offseason. He was coming off an injury-riddled campaign with the Portland Trail Blazers , rebuilding his stock early on and ahead of next year's loaded free agency class.

JJ Redick Giving Matisse Thybulle Freedom Defensively

Matisse Thybulle has always been one of the best perimeter defenders in the NBA. Thybulle was a two-time All-Defensive Second Team selection with the Philadelphia 76ers early in his career.

The Australian-American forward then struggled to stay healthy with the Portland Trail Blazers before joining the Los Angeles Lakers in the offseason.

And one of the reasons why Thybulle has flourished defensively is because of JJ Redick's decision to give him freedom on that end of the ball.

"It's no different than a highly unique offensive player and giving them freedom to be creative," Redick said via Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register . "You've got to be able to do it within our system. … He's got the freedom to be himself, and we know he's going to make more good happen than bad."

The Lakers are back in action on Monday, welcoming the Utah Jazz back for a rematch at the Crypto.com Arena.

articles.title: Louisville City FC falls to Sacramento club on penalties in USLC Final
articles.summary: After each squad put up one goal through extra time, Sacramento Republic FC edged out LouCity on penalty kicks, 4-3, to win its second USLC title.
articles.body:
On the final penalty kick of the match, Ryan Spaudling sealed it for Sacramento Republic FC to win the USL Championship Final.

While the USL Championship's title match was in California, Lynn Family Stadium wasn't empty. Fans in purple brought blanked and piled onto the pitch with their blankets and snacks to watch Louisville City FC and Sacramento Republic take it all the way to penalty kicks.

Just two minutes after a shot by Brandon Dayes grazed over the top of the goal, Sacramento Republic turned and scored first. Cal Jennings, who has scored seven goals in eight career games against LouCity, put his team up 1-0 in the 14th minute.

It didn't take much time for Louisville to strike back, when Ray Serrano cleaned up a shot at the net to tie the match 1-1 in the 31st minute. After Serrano's goal, fans at Lynn Family Stadium began to run around the field, doing their own scoring celebrations.

Louisville City FC faces Sacramento Republic in USLC Final. See photos

Both sides continued to attack throughout the second half, but neither team could break through. In the final moments before extra time, Aiden McFadden had a chance off of a free kick with Sacramento's goalkeeper on the ground, but his header drifted just far right, ultimately leading to extra time.

While both sides had their opportunities, the tie could not be broken, and the match headed to penalty kicks, with LouCity as the first squad to shoot.

Both sides made their first try and failed on their second. LouCity and Sacramento then each made their third to keep it tied as two makes apiece.

Louisville's fourth penalty, kicked by Tola Showunmi, was blocked, while Sacramento's Kyle Edwards capitalized to give his team the advantage.

Zach Duncan nailed the fifth shot to keep his team alive, but Ryan Spaulding put the nail in the coffin to secure the the USL Championship title for Sacramento Republic.

articles.title: Game Thread: Old Dominion vs. UConn|3:30 p.m. on CBS Sports Network
articles.summary: The Huskies’ are favored as they go for their sixth win of the season.
articles.body:
The Huskies will celebrate Senior Day in their last home game of the 2026 season against Old Dominion.

UConn looks to build on last week's 46-22 rout of JMU in Saturday's matchup against another Sun Belt team. In a much-needed victory, the team returned to a balanced offense and relentless defense. After their 24-point blowout, Connecticut jumped six national rankings to No. 26 in total offense, averaging 437.3 yards per game (249.4 passing, 187.9 rushing). They also leaped six national rankings to No. 95 in total defense, conceding 386.2 yards per meeting (248.8 passing, 137.8 rushing). Now, ODU's top-45 nationally ranked defense stands in the way of the Huskies' bowl eligibility.

"I think for the most part, that was our most complete game from an effort standpoint of things and just trying to impose our will for 60 minutes," head coach Jason Candle said when discussing last week's win.

Heading into the clash, UConn is favored (-13.5) for the first time since Week 7 against UMass. This year, Connecticut has gone two-for-two as the front-runner (Lafayette, UMass). Last week, the Huskies stalled the Dukes' offense, igniting a 36-9 run to win their second of seven underdog battles.

ODU's 2026 campaign hasn't been sunshine and rainbows, but they beat Coastal Carolina 21-8 last weekend, snapping their three-game losing streak. Quarterback Jaxon Potter, who has started the last three matches, completed 17 of 30 (56.7%) passes for 150 yards, an interception, and a touchdown. Potter is seen as a pocket passer, drop-back gunslinger, who rushed for -42 yards in the past four bouts.

Backup shot-caller, Quinn Henicle, also took the field and went four-for-four for 45 passing and 13 rushing yards for an end zone appearance. Henicle is a run-first player who started in five of the Monarchs' first six games and accumulated 64.6 yards per contest.

In the backfield, Devin Roche led with 46 rushing yards, gaining 2.6 yards per carry. In the air, tight end Leon Haughton Jr. hauled in six receptions for 67 yards and a touchdown. Trailing behind him, Josh Rodriguez posted 53 yards. Defensively, Old Dominion is aggressive, creating turnovers on the front with an experienced secondary. They currently rank No. 42 nationally in total defense, recovering 12 fumbles, with eight forced fumbles, 10 interceptions, and 25 sacks.

articles.title: Ferris State football wins 42nd straight after national TV spotlight
articles.summary: Ferris State football won its 42nd straight game, this time over Truman State, in the first round of the NCAA Division II playoffs.
articles.body:
BIG RAPIDS – Maybe, it was a Big Noon hangover.

After hosting Fox's "Big Noon Kickoff" pregame show outside of Top Taggert Field – the first time a college pregame show broadcast from a Division II school – the Ferris State Bulldogs came out sluggish in their first-round NCAA playoff game against Truman State on Saturday, Nov. 21.

The No. 1-ranked and two-time defending national champion Bulldogs made mistakes, blew a couple scoring opportunities and had a fumble, as Truman State took a 6-3 lead into the second quarter.

But as crews were tearing down the Fox set, the Bulldogs came alive, rolling to a 45-14 victory in front of 8,630 fans, their biggest crowd of the season.

Ferris will play Findlay in the second-round game in Big Rapids on Saturday, Nov. 28. Findlay won its first-round game by beating Augustana, 23-20, by kicking a field goal in overtime to advance. Grand Valley State also advanced, and would meet rival Ferris in the quarterfinals if both win next Saturday.

The Bulldogs were led by Chase Carter, a junior quarterback from Orlando, who completed 18 of 29 passes for 212 yards and two touchdowns. He also led the team in rushing with 17 carries for 93 yards.

Tarik Bower, a sophomore wide receiver from Corunna, caught five passes for 72 yards. And Taariik Brett, a senior, caught five passes for 42 yards and ran it four times for 72.

Trace Corlew, a sophomore defensive back from Gladwin, led the Bulldogs with 10 tackles. And Ryan Ahern, a sophomore linebacker from Rockford, added seven tackles.

Ferris State held Truman State to 80 yards rushing and 146 yards passing. Truman State quarterback Dylan Hair completed 11 of 20 passes for 146 yards with a touchdown and interception.

The Bulldogs have now won 42 consecutive games, an NCAA Division II record − Ferris State's last loss came Aug. 31, 2024, in its 2024 season opener to Pittsburg State (Kansas).

And Ferris has won four of the past five D-II national titles.

"It's great coaches," Ferris State coach Tony Annese said on the pregame show. "I've had two coaches that've been here since I've been here since in 2012, and then it's great players. It's recruiting, getting good players here. We've got something like 28 kids from Florida, so we go all over the nation to get recruits. And then it's player development. It's absolutely 100% player development."

The D-II national championship game is Dec. 19 at 4 p.m. ET in McKinney, Texas.

The Bulldogs are attempting to become the second D-II program with three straight titles, joining North Alabama in 1993-95.

articles.title: Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy Gets Coach to Take Blame for Costly Mistake
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are trending upward offensively. They have scored 35 points in back-to-back games, and put up 28 against the vaunted Denver Broncos’ d...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are trending upward offensively.

They have scored 35 points in back-to-back games, and put up 28 against the vaunted Denver Broncos' defense in Week 8. Kansas City's rushing attack has been dominant, and the passing game has had an uptick recently. However, one key player remains under scrutiny.

Kansas City Chiefs ST Coordinator Dave Toub Takes Blame for WR Xavier Worthy's Mistake

Worthy has struggled to take the next step in his development this season. He did not record a single catch on three targets last week against the Atlanta Falcons, including one that he dropped once he made contact with the ground.

His miscues spread to the special teams unit. During an onside kick attempt by Atlanta, the ball bounced over Worthy's head, and he did not make much of an attempt to make a play on it, resulting in a Falcons recovery. While speaking to the media this past week, special teams coordinator Dave Toub took the bullet for Worthy.

"I'm going to blame myself," Toub said. "We thought the kicker was going to kick something by the numbers. That's what the scouting report was on him. But, they lined up wide. I saw it, and I thought we were going to be ok. I could have called a timeout. I could have told Worthy to widen out. That's my fault."

Worthy Needs to Have Big Game to Silence Critics

As a former first-round draft pick, Worthy has been under the microscope every week. He's had some solid performances, recording five or more receptions in three games this season. However, his record-setting 4.21 40-yard dash speed has not translated on the field.

Worthy has caught just one pass that has gone over 20 yards. Despite his speed, he struggles to get separation against man coverage. If coach Andy Reid doesn't manufacture touches for him, Worthy doesn't typically produce.

With Josh Downs now in the mix , Worthy could slide down the depth chart. That may not be a bad thing, though. Having Downs and Rashee Rice as the top two receivers, along with an emerging Cyrus Allen, Worthy can slide under the radar and be used more for gadget type plays. He could also get into the mix more as a return specialist.

articles.title: Colin Simmons injury update: Texas star edge rusher won't play vs. Arkansas
articles.summary: Colin Simmons, the Texas football defensive standout, won't take the field Saturday in Austin.
articles.body:
Texas football will be without its top defensive player Saturday during the Longhorns' last regular-season game this year at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium.

Edge rusher Colin Simmons is ruled out for Saturday's game against Arkansas as he continues to manage a right-ankle sprain. The junior injured his ankle in Texas' loss to Florida last month, and he missed Texas' wins in subsequent games against Ole Miss and Mississippi State. Simmons played just 18 snaps against Missouri and did not register a tackle, though he recorded eight tackles in last week's win at LSU.

Simmons leads the SEC and ranks No. 2 nationwide with 10.5 sacks this season. No SEC player has more tackles for loss, and Simmons' excellence earned him a spot this week as one of three nominees across college football for the Bronko Nagurski Trophy, an honor given at the end of each season to the sport's best defensive player. The Dallas native hopes to become the third Texas player to ever win the Nagurski Trophy, joining linebacker Derrick Johnson (2004) and Brian Orakpo (2008).

Kickoff for Saturday's game is set for 2:30 p.m. CT.

articles.title: Gophers beat Northwestern with last-second field goal to become bowl-eligible
articles.summary: Minnesota found a way to earn its sixth win of the season.
articles.body:
It wasn't immediate results, but Minnesota's decision to move on from Greg Harbaugh Jr. as offensive coordinator yielded enough points to sneak past Northwestern 20-17 after another game-winning field goal from Luke Drzewiecki.

The Gophers' offense didn't have much explosiveness in the first half, but they also didn't make any huge mistakes. They were able to get into field goal range for two long attempts, but Drzewiecki missed from 48 and 53 yards. After starting the season 15 of 15, he has now missed four of his last six attempts.

Northwestern's offense wasn't much better, but another blatant coverage bust in Minnesota's secondary set up a 49-yard touchdown pass. The Gophers played some bad football in the first half, but only trailed 7-0 heading into the locker room.

Minnesota began the second half with something to prove. Drake Lindsey began the half 6 of 9 for 55 yards and two touchdowns. An Anthony Smith strip-sack and Darius Taylor's longest rush since Week 1 set them up in prime position, and they took advantage.

After a third-quarter field goal from Northwestern, Minnesota opted to pull out a trick play that nearly ended in disaster, but the Gophers were bailed out. Drzewiecki broke his cold streak with a 49-yard field goal to give Minnesota a 17-10 lead.

The Gophers' defense needed to make one more stop as Northwestern took over on its own 30-yard line with 2:54 left in the game, but it couldn't. The Wildcats tied the game with just 19 seconds left on the clock.

Minnesota had one timeout left in its back pocket, and that's all it needed. Lindsey found Noah Jennings on a 34-yard throw-and-catch to set up another game-winning field goal from Drzewiecki, and Minnesota won 20-17.

Taylor finished with 15 carries for a season-high 108 yards. Smith essentially matched his season-long production in tackles for loss and sacks on Saturday. They're two building blocks for this Gophers roster, and they finally performed like it.

Saturday's win gives everyone within the Gophers' program an opportunity to take a deep breath. They snapped a three-game losing streak, and they're officially bowl-eligible at 6-5. They will look to finish the regular season strong next Friday night against rival Wisconsin on the road at 6:30 p.m. CT.

articles.title: Will Shane Steichen be back in 2027?
articles.summary: After the 2025 season ended, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both G.M.
articles.body:
After the 2025 season ended, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both G.M. Chris Ballard and coach Shane Steichen on notice that much was expected in 2026.

Then, one day after the Colts lost to the Titans in Week 6, she fired Ballard and kept Steichen.

Nearly five weeks later, Steichen remains. After next Sunday's game against the Giants, the Colts will enter their bye. That's typically the best time for an in-season coaching change, since it gives the interim coach maximum time to get up to speed before the next game.

Creating a vacancy with six weeks left in the regular season carries a separate benefit. The team can get a head start on searching for the replacement. And if ownership already knows the coach will be fired after the season ends, it makes no sense to delay that part of the process.

So here's the question. Will Irsay-Gordon bring Steichen back in 2027?

It makes no sense to keep a new G.M. from hiring a new coach. Every G.M. arrives with a wish list of coaches who would be pursued, if/when the position is vacant. It makes plenty of sense to give a new G.M. an immediate vacancy to fill.

But what about the Colts this year has made sense? The firing of the G.M. left the team without a seasoned, experienced executive to navigate the strategy of making, or not making, trades. They quickly moved guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. They rejected offers for running back Jonathan Taylor and quarterback Daniel Jones. They moved two starting receivers — Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — on the day of the trade deadline.

Steichen has been operating for much of the season with one hand tied behind his back. Now, he'll have both wrists secured. Whatever the decision will be as to Steichen, it's unfair to base it on the team's overall performance since the Nelson and Buckner trades.

Before that point, they took the Chiefs to overtime in Kansas City. They beat the Texans. They manhandled the Commanders in London. They took the Vikings to the limit in Minnesota.

Although the signs point to Steichen eventually being fired, the fact that he's still there now means he could still be there later. The new G.M. may be expected to work with him.

It's ultimately the owner's call. And the owner may have strong feelings about Steichen's skills and abilities, based on the fact that she's on the sideline every week.

If she was upstairs, she'd likely be hearing criticism of the head coach during the game. Instead, she's watching him in his element. And she hasn't fired him yet.

Throw in the fact that a new coach may not be as welcoming to the owner's presence in the bench area, and she may be even more inclined to give Steichen (who's fine with it) another chance. Especially since she systematically began making his job much more difficult the moment the Colts traded Nelson and Buckner.

Moving forward, it'll be virtually impossible. The fact that Steichen has survived this long could mean that he'll survive whatever comes next.
